stories.Headline: Investors see bright prospects for AI applications in China - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Investors at the 5th Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit in Hong Kong said they see bright prospects for AI applications in China. The summit concluded on Wednesday, November 5, 2026. Zhang Lei, founder of Hillhouse Investment, spoke about the need for AI to deliver productivity. James Lydotes, chief investment officer of equities at a New York-based investment firm, told Xinhua that China is going to lead in physical AI.

Zhang said investors now expect AI to be applied in every industry, including manufacturing, health care, services and consumption. He said Asia will play a big role because it has more solid use cases than everywhere else. Lydotes said U.S. frontier labs and China are the biggest sources of AI innovation. He said he will be closely watching developments in factory automation in China to cash in on relevant investment.

China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology said late last month that it is drafting policies for next-generation smart manufacturing. The measures aim to deepen the integration of artificial intelligence and manufacturing. They are meant to integrate AI across the entire manufacturing chain and develop new manufacturing models. The ministry said these models would help firms cut costs, raise efficiency and better meet diverse market demands.

The summit took place as the AI race enters what the article calls a "show me the money" phase, with calls for returns from mounting capital expenditure. Zhang tied this to productivity, saying AI has to have some productivity. Lydotes pointed to China's advanced manufacturing facility as the reason he expects it to lead in physical AI. The article does not say what happens next beyond the ministry's drafting of the policies.

Articles.Title: Investors see bright prospects for AI applications in China - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Chinese premier calls for people-centered internet development amid AI advances - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Chinese Premier Li Qiang called for a more people-centered approach to internet development on Tuesday, speaking at the opening ceremony of the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit in Wuzhen, east China's Zhejiang Province. He noted that the conference has now been held for 13 consecutive years. He said the internet is undergoing an intelligent transformation as it increasingly integrates with artificial intelligence and other technologies. About 1,800 participants attended the opening ceremony, including government officials, representatives of international organizations such as the United Nations, global internet companies, experts and scholars.

Li said the ultimate purpose of internet development must be to promote the all-round development of people. He stressed that internet-related technologies should enhance human capabilities, expand choices, affirm human value and improve well-being, rather than make humans subordinate to technology or worsen disparities in human development. He called for joint efforts to build a community with a shared future in cyberspace. He said China will continue to pursue innovation through openness, promote technology transfer and knowledge sharing, and work with other countries to foster an open, inclusive and dynamic digital innovation ecosystem.

On digital security, Li said China will respect the legitimate cybersecurity concerns of all other countries and work with them to address security challenges. He also said China opposes the creation of a digital iron curtain. He pledged that China will actively implement the Global Development Initiative and support Global South countries in building digital infrastructure and enhancing their digital technology capabilities. Following the opening, Li visited the Light of Internet Expo and Wuzhen's World Internet Science and Technology Museum.

Articles.Title: Chinese premier calls for people-centered internet development amid AI advances - Xinhua

stories.Headline: China and WIPO sign memorandum to boost cooperation on AI, copyright, and cultural heritage protection
stories.Summary:
China's National Copyright Administration and the World Intellectual Property Organization signed a bilateral memorandum of understanding on cooperation on Monday in Dunhuang, Gansu province. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges, research and cooperation on artificial intelligence, copyright in the digital and online environment, the creative economy and industry, and the protection of traditional folk art. The signing was reported by China Daily on November 4, 2026. The memorandum builds on existing training programs between the two sides.

Under the memorandum, the two parties will explore a long-term and stable talent development mechanism and promote copyright services for the real economy. China's National Copyright Administration said the memorandum deepens cooperation and matters greatly for China's research on frontier copyright issues, its participation in global copyright governance and its international influence. On the same Monday, the two sides agreed to carry out project cooperation in Chongqing and Jincheng, Shanxi province. That work will explore ways and mechanisms for using copyrights and related intellectual property tools to support folk literature, art and cultural tourism.

The two sides will use their respective strengths and pool domestic and international resources to enhance the integrated development of copyright-enabled folk art and tourism. They aim to drive local industry upgrades and inject new momentum into the innovation of traditional Chinese cultures. The China Daily report gives no further details on funding or timelines for the projects. It also does not name the officials who signed the memorandum.

A separate China Daily report says shared risks from artificial intelligence are creating incentives for the United States and China to cooperate on safety despite political differences and competition. Steve Westly, founder and managing partner of The Westly Group, a Silicon Valley venture capital firm, said the issues in AI will force a US-China agreement and the sooner it comes the better. Liang Min, managing director of Stanford University's Bits & Watts Initiative, said cooperation and competition can coexist and pointed to US-China work on nuclear power plant safety as a precedent. In September, both governments announced a bilateral dialogue on AI risks and benefits and agreed to establish a communication channel for AI incidents, with the next exchange set for November.

Articles.Title: China and WIPO sign memorandum to boost cooperation on AI, copyright, and cultural heritage protection - China Daily Global Edition

stories.Headline: AMD advances inclusive AI through open innovation and green computing
stories.Summary:
AMD received the 2026 World Internet Conference Distinguished Contribution Award for Innovative Breakthrough, China Daily reported on November 4, 2026. The company was founded in Silicon Valley in 1969 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It makes CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, adaptive system-on-chips, DPUs and software for cloud, edge and end-user devices. China is a key market for AMD, and AMD Greater China was established in 2004 with headquarters in Beijing.

AMD has an R&D team of more than 4,000 engineers across Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Taipei. In fiscal 2025 the company invested $8.091 billion in R&D, up 25 percent year-on-year and about 23 percent of annual revenue. It ranked 167th on the 2025 Fortune 500 list of the largest US companies and was named one of Fortune's World's Most Admired Companies. In 2024 it was included in TIME's list of the 100 Most Influential Companies. More than 2.1 million models on major open-source AI platforms can now run directly on AMD's open-source ROCm software platform, which in early 2026 added simultaneous support for Windows and Linux.

AMD Developer Cloud provides computing resources to developers worldwide. In July 2025 the company helped establish China's first ROCm laboratory in Nanjing, Jiangsu province. AMD has joined nearly 100 partners in developing UALink, an open industry standard for connecting AI accelerators in data centers, and the technology has been recommended to China's Open Data Center Committee. The company continues to drive collaborative innovation with partners including Meta, Microsoft, DeepSeek and Alibaba Cloud.

Articles.Title: AMD advances inclusive AI through open innovation and green computing - China Daily

stories.Headline: Guangxi AI enhances trade, farming, education
stories.Summary:
Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region is working to become a hub for artificial intelligence by using its closeness to Southeast Asia to sell digital services and change traditional industries. Runjian Co Ltd, a technology company, recently won a $200 million overseas order for its AI token services. The company runs the Wuxiang Yungu Token Factory in Nanning, the regional capital, where computing resources stay in China while overseas clients send large-model requests through open application programming interfaces. Clients pay based on the number of tokens they use.

The factory combines green energy, 800-volt high-voltage direct current and micro-channel liquid cooling, which cuts costs by more than 20 percent and raises capacity by 700 percent. It currently handles 200 billion tokens per hour, with a medium-term target of 2 trillion. Nanning was approved in 2026 as one of China's pilot cities for international data cooperation, and Runjian now has over 240 overseas employees and has delivered more than 80 computing and data center projects across ASEAN. The Nanning International Communications Gateway has 15 cross-border optical cables, keeping latency to major ASEAN nodes such as Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam at 20 to 30 milliseconds. Runjian also signed six ASEAN computing network infrastructure projects worth over 250 million yuan, about $37.5 million.

Zhao Hua, vice-president of Runjian, said China and ASEAN have great complementary potential in AI, with China holding a mature industrial ecosystem and large-scale model capabilities while ASEAN offers vast market demand as its enterprises move from basic digitalization to intelligent applications. He said the company's path is to use research and development from top-tier Chinese cities, integrate systems in Guangxi and deploy applications in ASEAN. Tang Liang, deputy director of the information center at the Beijing Academy of Educational Sciences, stressed the need for comprehensive policies on AI use. He said stronger technological oversight and ethics education should ensure that technological advancement goes hand in hand with ethical responsibility.

Guangxi is also using AI in farming, with a smart sugarcane farm in Chongzuo raising land utilization to 95 percent and cutting water and fertilizer use by over 20 percent. In Hengzhou, 180,000 mu of jasmine fields are on a digital platform where farmers photograph crops and an AI system diagnoses pests and diseases with 99 percent accuracy. At Youyiguan Port in Pingxiang, import and export value reached 513.6 billion yuan in the first eight months, up 31.2 percent year-on-year, and durian imports alone reached 620,000 tons. Minister of Education Huai Jinpeng announced plans on AI education in 2025, and primary and secondary schools in Beijing will soon offer at least eight class hours of AI instruction per academic year.

Articles.Title: Guangxi AI enhances trade, farming, education - China Daily

stories.Headline: Legal system must keep pace with AI growth
stories.Summary:
At the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit in Zhejiang province, cyberspace experts spoke on Wednesday at the Cyberspace Rule of Law Forum, which was held on the sidelines of the event under the theme "Law and AI for Good: World's Landscape and China's Practice." Renata Mielli, special adviser to Brazil's minister of state for science, technology and innovation, said AI adoption is moving much faster than society's ability to understand its consequences and regulate it. Keovisouk Solaphom, deputy minister of technology and communications of the Lao People's Democratic Republic, said his country attaches great importance to improving its legal system for AI. Liu Taizong, director of the economic crime prosecution department of the Supreme People's Procuratorate, said new AI issues such as the "algorithm black box," "data poisoning" and "AI hallucinations" have emerged one after another.

Mielli said existing data protection, consumer protection and constitutional safeguards in Brazil remain essential but are insufficient for the specific challenges of AI. She called for clear obligations on algorithmic impact assessments, nondiscrimination, human oversight and accountability throughout the AI value chain, and said regulation should not be seen as an obstacle to innovation. She said appropriate rules can create trust, legal certainty and better conditions for responsible technological development. She added that Brazil faces the challenge of accelerating its national AI strategy, strengthening domestic technological capabilities and establishing an effective regulatory framework.

Solaphom said Laos is moving step by step on a legal foundation that includes laws on cybersecurity and personal data protection, the amended law on digital technology and the decree on digital government. He said the first task is to review these instruments to see whether they address AI issues and then to determine where new ones are needed. He said no country can address these challenges alone and that they require extensive consultation, joint contributions and shared benefits. He added that countries should share legislative experience, safety standards and testing methods to improve compatibility among regulatory frameworks and better prevent misuse of AI in fraud and scams.

Liu said criminals are increasingly using deepfakes and generative large language models for illegal activities, threatening cybersecurity and social stability. He said the rapid development of AI and the upgrading of industry models require continuous updates to governance rules. He said prosecutorial agencies will work with legislative and administrative bodies to advance legal frameworks in the AI field, such as the AI law. He said whether AI serves humanity as a trustworthy, reliable and controllable tool or becomes a source of risks depends on using the rule of law to establish safeguards, guide technology toward positive uses and regulate its applications.

Articles.Title: Legal system must keep pace with AI growth - China Daily

stories.Headline: AI to drive next farming revolution
stories.Summary:
Chinese researchers are using artificial intelligence to speed up seed breeding, according to a China Daily report published on November 5, 2026. Sun Qixin, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering and a professor at China Agricultural University, is using computer simulations to predict plant growth from genetic code. He said this could accelerate crop breeding by up to hundreds of times, compared with labor-intensive work once done in the field. Sun said the technology could mark the start of a fundamental revolution in agricultural breeding.

Sun said three foundations are needed for the change: more comprehensive agricultural data, lower-cost genetic sequencing and more sophisticated models linking a plant's genetic makeup to its observable traits. He said sequencing the genome of an individual wheat plant once cost around 1 million yuan, about $150,000, while comparable work now costs about 100 yuan. He expected that within three to five years, accumulated technical data on major grain crops and livestock could support specialized intelligent breeding models. He said AI could eventually take over as much as 80 percent of the workload in certain stages of conventional breeding, and that about five years may be needed before the practical impact becomes more widely visible.

Chen Wei, president of China Agricultural University, said the changing nature of agriculture is reshaping demand for talent and the priorities of agricultural universities. He said the university is adjusting its programs and research priorities under a medium- and long-term strategy for the next five to 10 years, and has introduced new programs including biological breeding and intelligent science and technology. He said agricultural technologies should be affordable and practical for farmers, and that their value depends not only on scientific breakthroughs but also on whether farmers can use them conveniently and effectively. Du Jinyi, from the national rural vitalization publicity and education center, said a workforce able to operate advanced equipment, interpret data and manage sophisticated production systems is in urgent need.

The 15th Five-Year Plan for accelerating agricultural and rural modernization, released in June, emphasizes emerging and future industries in agriculture, the first time such a focus has been explicitly included in a national planning document. It calls for scaling up technologies and industries including intelligent breeding, new-energy agricultural machinery, the low-altitude economy in agriculture, agricultural bio-manufacturing and novel foods. An official from the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs said the initiatives are intended to foster new quality productive forces in agriculture, with measures including tax incentives for scientific and technological innovation. Qiu Tongwei, a professor at Nanjing Agricultural University, said emerging and future agricultural industries form the technological foundation of the country's strategy to become an agricultural powerhouse.

Articles.Title: AI to drive next farming revolution - China Daily Global Edition

stories.Headline: Tencent steps up AI investment to create broader social value
stories.Summary:
Tencent increased its research and development spending to 27.28 billion yuan, or about 4.1 billion dollars, in the second quarter of 2026, up 35 percent from a year earlier. Capital expenditure rose 176 percent year-on-year and 65 percent quarter-on-quarter to 52.78 billion yuan, which the company linked to more investment in artificial intelligence. By the end of June 2026, Tencent had published more than 98,000 patent applications and secured over 55,000 patent grants across major countries and regions. These patents cover AI, cloud computing, mobility and instant messaging.

Tencent uses a dual-track strategy of proprietary development and open source for its models. Since rebuilding its infrastructure in February 2026, its Hunyuan large language model has released a major update about every two months, including Hy3 preview, the official Hy3 release and Hy4 preview this year. Hy3 has a smaller parameter size but performs comparably to flagship models with two to five times as many parameters, and since its July launch it has ranked among the world's top three models by token consumption. Hy4 preview expanded its model size, context length and training data, was fully open-sourced on release and keeps affordable pricing, and the next Hy4 model is expected soon.

Tencent aims to make AI agents digital companions for its 1.4 billion users and a new source of productivity across industries. Its productivity agents WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy are growing quickly, and according to Analysys, WorkBuddy recorded 85.34 million monthly visits in September 2026, leading China's desktop AI office agent market. Combined visits for the two products exceeded 110 million, and WorkBuddy launched an open platform covering hardware, Buddy apps, experts, skills and connectors with more than 100 partners at launch. WeCom has launched its AI assistant Dayuan, Weixin's native AI assistant Xiaowei is expanding closed beta testing, and Yuanbao Search is now available to individual developers and enterprises through Tencent Cloud.

Tencent has made promoting sustainable innovations for social value a core development strategy, using digital technology and its platforms to address social needs. With the Jingdezhen authorities it developed Digital Jingdezhen: Porcelain Craft Adventure, described as the world's first mini-game themed around a World Heritage nomination, launched on July 25, 2026. The simulation game recreates key stages of Jingdezhen's porcelain industry during the Song, Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties from 960 to 1911. It combines AI-generated 3D porcelain, interactive AI-powered non-player characters and AI-powered procedural content generation to recreate historical scenes, letting players explore traditional porcelain-making techniques and the city's ceramic heritage.

Articles.Title: Tencent steps up AI investment to create broader social value - China Daily

stories.Headline: No more ‘heads-up’ tracking: Chinese university scraps AI attention system amid privacy backlash
stories.Summary:
Nanjing University said on Wednesday that it had stopped tracking how often students looked up during class, after an AI-powered "smart classroom" system drew widespread attention online. The controversy began when students received a notice that the school would use its newly upgraded system to monitor attendance in certain courses over a one-week period. A screenshot then circulated online showing surveillance footage alongside data on late arrivals, attendance rates and the proportion of students looking up. Concerns grew after a teacher reportedly told a class group chat that attendance data could affect participation grades or even lead to exam results being cancelled.

Cover News reported that the university awarded a contract worth more than 31.52 million yuan, or about 4.4 million dollars, to upgrade 113 classrooms at its Xianlin campus. Tender documents listed technical requirements including facial detection, facial recognition, AI-based headcounts and tracking of how often students looked up. Some students told media the university had not sought their consent before introducing the system, raising concerns that their facial data could be accessed by the university or technology companies. Others said that even without facial recognition, having their attention monitored made them uncomfortable.

In a statement, the university's undergraduate education office and IT department denied that attendance was linked to grades or that the system was introduced in response to inspections by higher-level authorities. The university said the system did not collect biometric data such as facial features or use facial recognition technology. It said the project aimed to modernize teaching facilities, support livestreamed lectures and cross-campus interactions, and allow lessons to be recorded and replayed, and that it was reviewed by experts and went through public bidding under government procurement rules. The university said that without authorization the system does not collect facial or other biometric information or conduct facial recognition in teaching applications, and that it is currently no longer collecting data on the proportion of students looking up.

The university said images circulating online were personal screenshots taken during online teaching supervision at its Suzhou campus in May this year, rather than live surveillance footage from the current system. The controversy has fueled a broader debate over the growing use of AI in higher education, with critics questioning whether students' engagement can be measured by how often they look up. Critics warned that such technologies risk turning classrooms into spaces of constant algorithmic surveillance, according to the Paper. The university pledged to continue putting students first and to protect their privacy while using digital and intelligent technologies to support learning.

Articles.Title: No more ‘heads-up’ tracking: Chinese university scraps AI attention system amid privacy backlash - Global Times

stories.Headline: When Singles’ Day shoppers start stocking up on AI tokens, the time has changed: Global Times editorial
stories.Summary:
During this year's Singles' Day shopping festival, Chinese consumers found a new item on their shopping lists: AI tokens. Tmall and JD.com each introduced AI token sections bringing together services from Alibaba Cloud, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Zhipu AI. One livestream recorded sales of 2 trillion tokens in just half an hour. The Global Times editorial said this is a phenomenon rarely seen anywhere else in the world, and foreign media have noticed it with curiosity and astonishment.

The editorial said AI tokens are no longer simply an overseas concept copied in China. It said token-based consumption has grown from China's large digital consumer market, active user base and mature industrial ecosystem. According to OpenRouter, a global AI model aggregation platform, Chinese large language models have led US models in token usage for 27 consecutive weeks, including the week of October 26 to November 1. More than one-third of the tokens used by enterprises in Global South countries come from Chinese models.

The editorial argued that the decisive factor in AI competition is whether companies can consistently deliver reliable, practical AI services at reasonable costs. It said a 2025 KPMG survey covering 47 countries found that Chinese people were among the most optimistic about AI. It credited this to China's rise in national strength and to broad improvements in education and culture over several decades. It said the transformation was driven by practical efforts so that ordinary people can share in the benefits of technological progress, not by exploitation, coercion or barriers.

The editorial also described how Chinese households once prized watches, bicycles, sewing machines and radios, and later televisions, refrigerators and washing machines. It said few could have imagined that China would later help define new forms of consumption and new standards in the digital wave. It said the rapid uptake of open-source large language models and the deployment of humanoid robots in industry tell a different story from Western doubts about China's ability to innovate. It said the "AI Plus" initiative is empowering sectors such as education, healthcare, elderly care, culture and tourism, employment and consumer services.

Articles.Title: When Singles’ Day shoppers start stocking up on AI tokens, the time has changed: Global Times editorial - Global Times

stories.Headline: China’s daily AI token use surges to 140 trillion: Wuzhen blue book
stories.Summary:
China's daily use of artificial intelligence tokens reached 140 trillion in March, according to a blue book released on Wednesday at the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit in Zhejiang Province. Tokens are the basic units that large language models process when handling a prompt or generating a response. The blue book, the China Internet Development Report 2026 and the World Internet Development Report 2026 were compiled by the Chinese Academy of Cyberspace Studies. The China report cited monitoring data from the National Data Administration.

A separate report from the China Internet Network Information Center showed that China had more than 700 million generative AI users as of the end of June, more than half of the population. China's market for enterprise AI agents reached 21.2 billion yuan, or 3.17 billion dollars, in 2025. China's embodied AI market reached about 915 billion yuan in 2025, up 20.4 percent year on year. More than 140 Chinese companies made complete humanoid robots in 2025 and released more than 330 products, and AI is already used at more than 30 percent of manufacturing firms above designated size.

Industry analyst Liu Dingding told the Global Times that token use is rising as people use AI more often and give it harder tasks, and that producing a short drama with AI can consume far more tokens than drafting an article. He said companies need to see that AI saves money or helps them get more work done to keep paying for it after a trial. Unitree Robotics founder Wang Xingxing said at a side forum that 2027 would likely be a turning point for the robotics industry or the AI models that power robots. He described the last few millimeters as the biggest hurdle for embodied AI, saying robots can pick up objects reliably but still struggle with finer control such as taking apart a smartphone or threading a needle.

The World report said AI was moving into the physical world and expanding the scope of scientific research, and it warned that uneven progress was widening the global digital divide. It said China is among the global front-runners in internet development, with advantages in industrial applications, the scale of the digital economy and infrastructure. As of June, 924 generative AI services had completed filing and 573 applications or features had completed registration. China had 47 AI computing facilities in the 10,000-card class as of the end of the first quarter of 2026.

Articles.Title: China’s daily AI token use surges to 140 trillion: Wuzhen blue book - Global Times

stories.Headline: China stocks surge as policy support boosts sentiment; AI tech shares lead rally
stories.Summary:
Chinese equities rebounded sharply on Wednesday, supported by policies aimed at stabilizing the capital markets and lifting investor confidence, with artificial intelligence and technology shares leading the gains. The STAR Composite Index, which tracks China's sci-tech innovation board, closed 9.9 percent higher at 1,525.31 points. More than 150 stocks on that board hit their daily price limit or rose more than 10 percent, according to the Securities Times. Chipmaker CXMT jumped 13.63 percent, with turnover above 20 billion yuan, or about 2.99 billion dollars.

Total A-share turnover reached 2.0519 trillion yuan, up 336.8 billion yuan from the previous session, and more than 4,600 stocks advanced. The People's Bank of China said on Wednesday it had cut the rate on its stock repurchase and share buy-back relending facility by 25 basis points to 1 percent, effective immediately. The facility is open to 21 national-level commercial banks and five systemically important city-level banks, covers 100 percent of eligible loans, has a one-year term and can be extended as banks need. Banks may add a reasonable margin on top of the relending rate and set their own maturities and pricing for such loans. The central bank also said it would fully meet banks' relending needs, after banks submitted quota applications totaling more than 200 billion yuan.

Li Chang'an, a professor at the University of International Business and Economics, said the rate cut would lower financing costs for listed companies and make share buybacks and stake increases easier when markets are relatively weak. He added that long-term market stability depends on deeper institutional reforms, including stricter IPO screening, improved delisting mechanisms and better dividend policies. Dong Shaopeng, a senior research fellow at Renmin University of China, said using tools such as stock repurchase and related refinancing to inject liquidity is both necessary and beneficial. He rejected foreign media claims that volatility is mainly driven by external shocks and sell-offs in technology and AI sectors, saying it largely reflects domestic market dynamics. Yang Delong, chief economist at First Seafront Fund, said the rally reflected both a technical rebound from oversold conditions and a policy-driven improvement in expectations.

The rate cut followed the central bank's announcement earlier this week that the relending program would become a permanent institutional arrangement, with the rate lowered from 1.25 percent to 1 percent. The program is one of two policy tools supporting the capital market, alongside the Securities, Funds and Insurance Companies Swap Facility. CXMT also announced a plan to raise its share repurchase from a range of 1 billion to 2 billion yuan to a range of 2.5 billion to 5 billion yuan, saying the proposal reflects confidence in its future development. The People's Bank of China, the National Financial Regulatory Administration and the China Securities Regulatory Commission had held two separate meetings aimed at stabilizing the capital market. Analysts said the market is expected to gradually shift from sentiment-driven trading to performance driven by fundamentals.

Articles.Title: China stocks surge as policy support boosts sentiment; AI tech shares lead rally - Global Times

stories.Headline: Analysis: Anthropic’s IPO Tests AI’s Growth Story Against Its Costs
stories.Summary:
Anthropic filed for a U.S. initial public offering on Oct. 26, disclosing rapid revenue growth and its first quarterly operating profit alongside nearly $800 billion in long-term computing commitments. The Claude developer plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, with trading expected to begin in mid-November after a roadshow. A U.S. hedge fund representative told Caixin the offering could raise $50 billion to $100 billion, though Anthropic has not announced an offering size or price range. Market expectations value the company above $1.5 trillion, below earlier estimates of $2 trillion.

First-half revenue reached $16.3 billion, up 1,300% from a year earlier, and annual revenue rose from $41 million in 2023 to $4.6 billion in 2025. Usage-based token charges generated $13.06 billion, or 80.2% of first-half revenue, while subscriptions contributed another $3.22 billion. Enterprise customers with at least $100,000 in trailing 12-month revenue rose from over 950 in September 2025 to over 11,900 a year later. First-half computing costs rose 283% to $8.95 billion, falling to 55% of revenue from 201% a year earlier.

Anthropic earned a second-quarter operating profit of $974 million, while its first-half operating loss was $693 million and its first-half GAAP net loss was $80.75 billion. Nearly $72.4 billion of that net loss reflected fair-value changes in convertible notes and derivative liabilities, not operating losses. Commitments to Amazon total $110 billion from May 2026 through April 2036, and many of the nearly $800 billion in commitments require payment even if unused. At June 30, Anthropic held $112.4 billion in cash and equivalents plus $19.3 billion in short-term investments.

Public investors will have limited governance influence, because a single Class F share held by an entity jointly owned by the seven founders carries non-dilutable 50.1% of shareholder voting power but no economic rights. The independent Long-Term Benefit Trust will appoint four of seven directors after the IPO, enabling it to remove executives or delay model releases on safety grounds. As a Delaware public-benefit corporation, Anthropic must balance shareholders' interests, affected people, and its responsible-AI mission, and it warned these objectives could conflict with financial performance. The listing follows OpenAI's September decision not to list this year, and on Oct. 26 AI infrastructure stocks rose, with Nvidia up 2.39%, CoreWeave up 1.76% and Amazon up 0.44%.

Articles.Title: Analysis: Anthropic’s IPO Tests AI’s Growth Story Against Its Costs - Caixin Global

stories.Headline: AI-Linked Breaches Mount as WorkOS, Northflank, Trigger.dev Disclose Hacks
stories.Summary:
Over the past month, hackers have hit at least a dozen AI developer platforms, including CommandCode, Northflank, Trigger.dev, Chainstack and WorkOS. The attackers appear to have been hunting for AI access tokens they could sell, and they used AI agents to speed up their intrusions. The incidents do not appear to be related, and the attackers got in through different routes, from stolen credentials to third-party dependencies and exploited vulnerabilities. Other victims named in the reporting include Andromeda, Brev (NVIDIA), Fireworks AI, Lightning AI, OpenCode, Railway, Warp and Zeabur, with the hackers mainly after stored customer secrets.

Chainstack, a blockchain infrastructure and Web3 services provider, was hit on October 26, and the attackers reached a development environment and parts of its production environment through a third-party component. The company said a database holding customer account information was accessed, including organization names, account holder names, member email addresses and password hashes. Node credentials may also have been exposed, and Chainstack told customers to rotate them. WorkOS, an API platform for building enterprise applications, said the hackers compromised an internal application used by its sales team on October 30.

The accessed data included names, email addresses, phone numbers, job titles, company affiliations, customer account histories, sales details, customer communications and information about customers' use of WorkOS products. The Cloud Security Alliance said intruders are reaching AI provider credentials through hosting platforms, evaluation services and developer consoles, and that because that layer holds credentials for many downstream customers, one intrusion can expose keys for many inference accounts at once. Wiz said the surge comes from LLM-jacking and LLM broker infrastructure, which make stolen AI access tokens easy to sell, and it expects more threat actors to turn to credential theft. Wiz also said it saw multiple threat actors using the same compromised keys, which suggests a strong market for this type of credential.

Chainstack and WorkOS both disclosed attacks that relied on the open source AI penetration testing framework Artex for automation, and multiple companies have linked attacks attributed to the Chinese APT Storm-0940 to the use of Artex. The reporting ties the trend to demand driven by distillation, which means training a cheaper model on the outputs of a more advanced one, notably alleged against Chinese AI labs. Wiz said it observed hackers abusing enterprise credentials compromised in these attacks, including two cases that shared an identical first unauthorized activity, which happened within 30 minutes of the reported credential access in the vendor breach. The articles do not say what happens next beyond Chainstack prompting customers to rotate node credentials.

Articles.Title: AI-Linked Breaches Mount as WorkOS, Northflank, Trigger.dev Disclose Hacks - SecurityWeek

stories.Headline: NTT Signs Multi-Year Deal With McLaren F1 Starting 2027 to Support Team on AI Security
stories.Summary:
NTT and McLaren Racing announced on November 4, 2026 that NTT will become an official partner of the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team for multiple years starting with the 2027 season. The deal centers on AI security and governance, with NTT supporting McLaren's push to become the team that most adeptly harnesses AI on the F1 grid. The two companies said they will also create engagement programs so NTT customers and F1 fans can experience NTT's technology firsthand. The partnership builds on earlier ties through NTT Docomo Business with the McLaren F1 team and NTT DATA with the Arrow McLaren IndyCar Team.

Under the agreement, NTT will help build a framework to manage the security risks that come with rapidly evolving AI technology, aiming for responsible AI use alongside faster innovation. The contract starts with the 2027 season and runs for multiple years, and the target team is the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team. The stated pillars of the collaboration are AI security and governance and engagement programs. McLaren Racing was founded in 1963 and first entered F1 in 1966, and it has won 23 F1 World Championship titles and more than 200 Grand Prix victories.

Akira Shimada, NTT's Representative Director, President and CEO, said he was delighted to announce the partnership and noted that F1 is a stage where wisdom from around the world gathers and the challenge to push the limits continues. He said McLaren and NTT share much in common, and that NTT aims to build on its experience as title sponsor of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES since 2019 and to accelerate global business with McLaren. McLaren CEO Zak Brown welcomed bringing NTT on board as an official partner and said AI holds enormous potential for motorsport and for McLaren's business. He said NTT's expertise will be a major support in introducing new technology in a responsible and safe manner.

For NTT, the deal is a chance to make an impression in overseas markets as it shifts beyond its role as a telecommunications carrier toward businesses centered on AI and security. For McLaren, getting a risk-management framework for expanding AI use from an outside specialist is expected to enhance its credibility in racing operations and business. F1 teams are increasingly using AI in data analysis and simulation, while handling confidential driving data and strategy information makes security and governance an unavoidable challenge. If NTT can show its presence in this area, the articles say, ripple effects into industries such as automotive and manufacturing can be expected, and the two companies' efforts toward the 2027 season could influence the standard for AI use in F1.

Articles.Title: NTT Signs Multi-Year Deal With McLaren F1 Starting 2027 to Support Team on AI Security - BigGo Finance

stories.Headline: Kyndryl CEO: AI Modernization Means Transforming IT Without Disruption
stories.Summary:
Kyndryl Chairman and CEO Martin Schroeter told analysts on Wednesday, during prepared remarks for the company's fiscal second-quarter 2027 conference call, that Kyndryl is expanding its AI capabilities and partner relationships to help customers modernize mission-critical IT infrastructure without disrupting operations. He said modernization demand is creating opportunities across consulting, public and private cloud, and agentic AI, as customers balance transformation with stability. He said customers trust Kyndryl to run and modernize their essential technology environments at scale, and rely on it to lead complex migrations, modernize applications and data, and deploy AI securely. Kyndryl is ranked No. 13 on CRN's 2026 Solution Provider 500.

The company this year expanded its AI innovation lab network to include Dallas and Luxembourg, joining its previous facility in Liverpool, England, where designers, forward-deployed engineers, and industry specialists test use cases, validate business outcomes, and develop roadmaps for scaling AI in existing environments. Schroeter said Kyndryl Bridge connects much of the company's work by bringing data insights, AI governance and orchestration into a single platform, giving people and increasingly agents the context to understand what is happening and determine the appropriate next action. Kyndryl next week plans to unveil a co-developed solution with ServiceNow that will combine AI-powered workflows with Kyndryl Bridge data, operational intelligence, and agents, and he previewed an AI sovereignty offering addressing customers' need to retain platform choice and data control. He said the expanded Broadcom relationship adds end-to-end VMware Cloud Foundation consulting for private-cloud modernization, and that Kyndryl Consult signings exceeded revenue over the past 12 months. He reaffirmed the full-year outlook and said the company is progressing toward its fiscal 2028 financial objectives.

Asked about Kyndryl Consult growth, Schroeter said there was a deceleration between the first and second fiscal quarters, but revenue tends to move up and down, and he expects the second quarter to be the low point of the year in constant currency growth for the business. Asked about potential softness in Europe, he said data sovereignty issues are important everywhere but especially in Europe, and those discussions are challenging for customers dealing with mission-critical systems in an ever-changing geopolitical world. He said Kyndryl plans to unveil a sovereignty approach next week, and that when the company brings innovation and expertise, customers are willing to make a move. He said Europe has been a little slower but is starting to come back in signings and revenue performance.

For the fiscal second quarter 2027, which ended September 30, Kyndryl reported total revenue of $3.65 billion, down 1.9 percent from $3.72 billion a year earlier. That included U.S. revenue of $980 million, up from $899 million; Japan revenue of $555 million, down from $581 million; revenue from Canada, the U.K., France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and Portugal of $1.18 billion, down from $1.25 billion; and revenue from the rest of the world of $939 million, down from $987 million. Total revenue beat analyst expectations by $80 million, according to Seeking Alpha. Kyndryl reported GAAP net earnings of $59 million, or 27 cents per share, down from $68 million, or 29 cents per share, and non-GAAP net income of $92 million, or 42 cents per share, up from $89 million, or 38 cents per share, which beat expectations by 4 cents per share.

Articles.Title: Kyndryl CEO: AI Modernization Means Transforming IT Without Disruption - CRN

stories.Headline: Kyndryl Q2 FY27 slides: margins expand as AI modernization drives signings
stories.Summary:
Kyndryl Holdings presented its second quarter fiscal 2027 earnings results on November 4, 2026, and its shares rose 37.25% to $17.76 after the presentation. The IT infrastructure services provider reported revenue of $3,651 million, down 1.9% from $3,721 million a year earlier, while the constant-currency decline was 0.8%. Adjusted EBITDA reached $699 million at a 19.1% margin, up 190 basis points from 17.2%, and adjusted pretax income was $150 million at a 4.1% margin, up 80 basis points. Adjusted earnings per share of $0.42 beat the consensus estimate of $0.41, and revenue beat by $10 million.

By segment, the United States generated $980 million with 9% growth, Principal Markets contributed $1,177 million, Strategic Markets added $939 million, and Japan accounted for $555 million. Kyndryl Consult revenue grew 8% to $3.6 billion on a last-twelve-months basis, and hyperscaler-related revenue surged 39% to $2.1 billion from $1.5 billion. Last-twelve-months signings for Kyndryl Consult reached $4.6 billion, including 43 deals greater than $50 million, 11 of them signed in the second quarter, and 154 deals above $10 million. First-half signings grew about 34% combined, with first-quarter signings up 50% and second-quarter signings up in the high 20% range.

The company said its progress against fiscal 2028 signposts was positive, citing a 5-point improvement in backlog trajectory, Kyndryl Consult signings of $4 billion versus $3.5 billion in revenue, and 8% priced margins on post-spin signings. It reported $1 billion in cumulative savings from Advanced Delivery initiatives powered by Agentic AI. Kyndryl earned the 2026 Google Cloud Global Partner of the Year Award for Infrastructure Modernization and was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Center Outsourcing Services. It also received partner of the year awards from Dell Technologies, HPE, and Cloudflare, and Microsoft gave it the Frontier Partner badge.

As of September 30, 2026, Kyndryl held $1.7 billion in cash and $4.8 billion in available liquidity, with net debt of $2.4 billion. Its net leverage ratio was 0.9x, up from 0.5x at the end of fiscal 2026 but still below its target of less than 1x adjusted EBITDA. The presentation described customer wins including a 16-year relationship with a global marketing services company, a 20-year partnership with a major European bank, and a 15-year relationship with a global luxury goods company. All three case studies emphasized expanding scope with long-standing customers.

stories.Headline: Kyndryl Prioritises Enterprise AI, Alliance-Led Growth and Partner Readiness
stories.Summary:
Kyndryl has set out four priorities for its channel strategy in 2027, according to Vikas Dua, Vice President and Application, Data and AI Practice Leader at Kyndryl India. The priorities are driving enterprise AI adoption, accelerating alliance-led growth, strengthening partner readiness and delivering outcome-led solutions. The company says the focus is on helping customers scale AI through AI-ready infrastructure, Agentic AI and AI-enabled operations. It also plans to strengthen partner capabilities through training and certifications across AI, Hybrid Cloud and Cybersecurity.

The programme is built around four key areas, the article says. It promotes joint business planning and co-creation so partners can align on account plans, develop solutions together and coordinate customer engagement. Partner enablement covers certifications, technical training and knowledge sharing to strengthen solution development and delivery. The programme also combines partner innovation with Kyndryl's enterprise IT transformation and services expertise, and encourages Enterprise AI collaboration on integrated solutions that meet enterprise requirements for security, scalability and operational readiness.

Dua said Kyndryl will co-create industry-specific solutions with partners, combining complementary technologies and services to deliver measurable business outcomes and long-term growth. He said the focus moving forward will be on deepening technology partnerships, strengthening joint go-to-market initiatives and scaling AI-led modernization solutions. He described the approach as positioning Kyndryl as an ecosystem orchestrator, bringing together the strengths of multiple technology partners. Through deeper alliances and co-innovation, he said, the goal is to accelerate modernization and AI adoption while addressing enterprise needs for security, resiliency and scalability.

stories.Headline: Legal AI Startup Harvey Has Held Early Talks About an IPO
stories.Summary:
Legal AI startup Harvey has taken early steps toward an initial public offering, according to two people familiar with the matter. The company, recently valued at $15.5 billion, has held preliminary talks with lawyers at Latham & Watkins about going public. One of those people said no listing is imminent, and Harvey is likely to watch how the coming wave of tech listings performs before deciding whether to proceed. Harvey declined to comment, and Latham & Watkins did not respond to a request for comment.

The idea of a four-year-old startup debuting on the public markets would have seemed far-fetched a year ago. Since then, SpaceX completed the largest IPO in history, and Anthropic could surpass it when it lists shares, potentially as soon as the week before Thanksgiving. OpenAI could follow in early 2027. Harvey said in September that it had crossed $400 million in annual recurring revenue, a figure that places it in the same range as Affirm and Snowflake at the time of their listings. This fall, the company raised $550 million in a round led by Diffusion and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with backers that include Goldman Sachs Alternatives and J.P. Morgan's Growth Equity Partners.

Harvey has also reshaped its leadership ahead of a possible listing. It hired Steve Zad, who helped guide cybersecurity company Rubrik through its 2024 IPO, as its first chief revenue officer. Other new hires include former Google executive Keith Enright as chief strategy officer and Rachel Hepworth as chief marketing officer. John LaBarre, the company's first legal hire, was promoted to chief legal officer, and Katie Burke became chief operating officer after helping take HubSpot public. The company's path to Wall Street also runs through one of its own customers, since Latham & Watkins signed a deal last year to roll out Harvey's software to all of its lawyers.

Harvey's rise comes after many investors had dismissed legal technology as a small market with only 1.3 million lawyers in the United States. Large language models changed that view, and cofounders Winston Weinberg and Gabe Pereyra began building software to read and write legal documents before ChatGPT launched. The company now has more than 3,500 customers, including 80% of the top 100 US law firms and 20% of the Fortune 500. Rival Legora raised $550 million at an $8.8 billion valuation last month, showing how intensely investors are pursuing the next Harvey. Latham & Watkins, which has advised on 186 offerings raising more than $101 billion since 2016, is the most active firm by deal count, according to Deal Point Data.

Articles.Title: Legal AI Startup Harvey Has Held Early Talks About an IPO - Business Insider

stories.Headline: Together AI Beats OpenRouter, Fireworks: $0.88/M [2026]
stories.Summary:
On November 4, 2026, shattered.io published a comparison of Together AI, Fireworks AI and OpenRouter, written by Tom Vance. It reported that Together AI and Fireworks AI sell tokens directly from their own GPU fleets, while OpenRouter is a routing layer that bills each request at the underlying provider's list price and collects a fee when customers buy credits. On the open models both clouds host, the standard rates match to the decimal, with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at $0.30 per million input tokens and $1.20 per million output tokens at either one. Meta's Muse Spark Open landed on Together AI on October 15 and on Fireworks AI on October 20, and OpenRouter rebuilt its default provider routing on October 28.

OpenRouter charges 5.5% on credit purchases under its Standard plan and 8% under Business, with a $0.80 minimum per purchase, and crypto payments carry a flat 5% fee. Its first $25,000 per month of list-price inference through a customer's own provider keys carries no fee, and usage above that costs 5%. Together AI charges no fee on serverless usage and has no minimums, with entry pricing per token, and its US endpoint multiplies input, cached input and output rates by 1.25. Fireworks AI advertises pay-per-token usage from $0.05 per million input tokens, with Priority adding 25% on Ember-1, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 20% on GPT-OSS 120B and 50% on Muse Spark Open and Qwen 3.8 Max, while Spot cuts 30% and Batch cuts 50% off input and output. Fireworks applies a 50% premium on US-only serverless for select models, waived on Muse Spark Open, and its fine-tuning starts at $0.50 per million training tokens.

Together AI's Post-Training, launched October 19, bills reserved GPU time, and its example of four trainer and four generator GPUs on B200-SXM at $11 per GPU-hour comes to $88 per hour, with a promotional rate valid until December 14, 2026. Together's dedicated H100 80GB runs $5.49 per hour, and Fireworks' On-Demand pricing is reportedly $13 per hour. OpenRouter's Auto Exacto re-evaluates providers every 5 minutes for tool-calling requests and is on by default, and on October 30 the company added Private Endpoints for Enterprise customers. A separate Quasa.io article from November 2, 2026 reported InferenceBench measurements: on GLM-5.2, Together's median time to first token was 291 ms against OpenRouter's 413 ms, with reported reliability of 93.5% against 99.1%, and on DeepSeek V4 Flash, OpenRouter led on output throughput, 101 against 67 tokens per second, and reliability, 100% against 91.9%.

The articles say the choice depends on the workload. Quasa.io said to choose Together AI when a fixed model on its inference service meets latency and reliability needs, and OpenRouter when an application benefits from selecting among providers, controlling a route's price or keeping another provider if one fails. Shattered.io said that if cost predictability matters, customers should pin a specific provider in the request rather than accept the default, because the 5.5% fee is a known quantity while an unpinned router is not. It also noted that OpenRouter's secondary coverage reportedly puts the cost increase from the routing change near 6%, though that figure does not come from OpenRouter and the sources checked could not confirm it.

Articles.Title: Together AI Beats OpenRouter, Fireworks: $0.88/M [2026] - shattered.io

stories.Headline: ZS Expands Agentic AI Capabilities in ZAIDYN for Life Sciences
stories.Summary:
ZS announced on November 4, 2026 that it had expanded agentic AI capabilities in ZAIDYN, its connected suite of applications for the life sciences industry. The company, a global management consulting and technology firm based in Evanston, Illinois, built ZAIDYN in 2021 with AI at its core. The suite offers more than 30 modules used by life sciences companies, including 80% of the top 20, in over 100 countries. The new agents can sense signals, analyze information, generate insights, recommend actions and automate approved activities within defined guardrails.

The expansion applies the new agentic capabilities across commercial, personalization, medical and patient workflows. ZAIDYN is designed to deliver value in three ways: accelerating planning and insight generation, responding to market signals, and automating workflows. Because the applications are connected, they can coordinate data, insights, decisions and actions across functions when the work requires it. The suite is designed to work with companies' existing technology foundations, including CRM and data lakehouse systems, and organizations can operate it themselves or have ZS operate it on their behalf.

Sunil Dixit, chief product officer at ZS, said clients face declining HCP access, pricing pressures and more than $200 billion in sales facing loss of exclusivity, while preparing for a promising pipeline of new launches. He said AI offers a disruptive technology to respond to these market challenges, and that ZAIDYN can help clients use intelligence more quickly so teams can accelerate commercialization and deepen engagement with patients and providers. He added that the suite retains the guardrails and human oversight a regulated industry like life sciences demands. ZS said people stay in control of decisions that require human judgment.

ZS was founded in 1983 and has more than 15,000 employees in over 40 offices worldwide. The company said the evolution of ZAIDYN's agentic AI capabilities is already earning industry recognition, with Everest Group naming ZS a Luminary in its 2026 Innovation Watch assessment on agentic AI in life sciences commercial. ZS described ZAIDYN as a key part of its strategy of helping organizations embed transformational AI into workflows and scale better decision-making across the enterprise. The company said the suite is supported from strategy and implementation through change management and ongoing operations.

Articles.Title: ZS Expands Agentic AI Capabilities in ZAIDYN for Life Sciences - HPCwire

stories.Headline: Lazarus AI Raises $43M to Advance Independent AI
stories.Summary:
Lazarus AI announced on November 4, 2026, that it has raised $43 million in funding. The round included participation from QBE, Mucker Capital, Motivate Ventures, State Farm Ventures, Wave Function Ventures, Indelible Solutions, Joyance Partners, AllegisNL Capital, One Way Ventures, AngelList, Techstars, Plug and Play and others. The Boston-based company applies AI to consequential problems while customers keep control of data, models, deployment and economics. Lazarus says it is trusted by insurers, government agencies and technology companies to run production AI.

The platform runs on-premises, in sovereign environments or in a customer's cloud, with no per-token charges and no rebuild when models or hardware change. In a modeled high-volume scenario, it cut annual operating costs 78% versus pay-per-use frontier models. Its Applied Intelligence System cites every finding to its source page and has raised field-level accuracy 12.5 points over standalone models across 150 customer use cases. Clearwing finds vulnerabilities in source code, reproduces them, grades the evidence and proposes a fix, while engineers decide when it lands. Constructor recovers business logic from decades-old systems and generates modern code proven equivalent to the original, now in pilots with two of the world's largest mainframe makers.

Alex Panait, CEO of Lazarus AI, said the opportunity in AI is enormous, and so is the question of control, including who chooses the models, where data runs, how costs behave and whether an organization can still change direction. He said customers keep sensitive data inside their walls, approve every model change and see the evidence behind every result. Lazarus will use the funding to expand strategic partnerships, invest in R&D and bring new products to market. The company serves insurers, healthcare, government and financial institutions across North America, Asia-Pacific and Europe.

Articles.Title: Lazarus AI Raises $43M to Advance Independent AI - HPCwire

stories.Headline: NCDIT issues RFP for AI platforms & services
stories.Summary:
The North Carolina Department of Information Technology, known as NCDIT, has issued a Request for Proposals, numbered RFP No. 800000 000, for generative artificial intelligence platforms and related services for use across state government. The solicitation is a key step in carrying out the state's AI Strategic Roadmap, which calls on state government to modernize and build trustworthy ways to use AI tools. The announcement was reported in a November 5, 2026 article from the Greater Fayetteville Business Journal. The RFP is now open on the state's Electronic Vendor Portal.

The procurement goes beyond the technology itself, since it also seeks implementation support, AI literacy, and job-specific training so state employees can use these tools safely and with confidence. Any tools acquired through the award must operate within the state's existing AI governance, including the N.C. State Government Responsible Use of AI Framework and Executive Order 24. The state is aiming to give agencies a simpler path to secure, trusted AI tools. The stated goal is to help employees spend more time serving residents.

NCDIT Secretary and State Chief Information Officer Nate Denny, speaking in a press release, said the state is always looking for ways to deliver government services to North Carolinians better and faster. He said that giving agencies a simpler path to secure, trusted AI tools can help employees focus more on serving the public. The article does not provide further remarks from other officials. The department's role in running the procurement is reflected in the solicitation itself.

Vendors have a set schedule to follow for the solicitation. Questions from vendors are due November 9, 2026, and proposals are due November 30, 2026. Interested vendors are directed to the solicitation for full requirements and instructions. More information on North Carolina's responsible use of AI in state government is available on the state's AI website.

Articles.Title: NCDIT issues RFP for AI platforms & services - Greater Fayetteville Business Journal

stories.Headline: Bybit CEO Ben Zhou: AI, Tokenization and Connected Infrastructure to Reshape the Future of Finance
stories.Summary:
Bybit Co-founder and CEO Ben Zhou spoke at Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026, which took place on November 4th, 2026, according to a Chainwire announcement dated the same day. He appeared in a main-stage fireside chat titled "Bridging the Divide: The Next Chapter of TradFi & Crypto Convergence." Bybit says it is trusted by more than 80 million users worldwide. Zhou used the session to share his views on how artificial intelligence, asset tokenization and connected financial infrastructure are reshaping financial services.

Zhou said the next stage of finance is not about traditional finance and crypto replacing one another but about making them work together. He said AI, tokenization and connected infrastructure can help users reach more markets and services more efficiently. He noted that putting assets on-chain is only a starting point, and that wider adoption needs clear investor rights, dependable custody and enough liquidity. He also said that as AI moves from giving information to starting financial actions, platforms will need stronger permissions, better monitoring and more refined user controls.

Zhou stressed that greater access and efficiency must go hand in hand with security, risk management and regulatory compliance. He said platforms must build these safeguards into their infrastructure as they expand beyond trading to serve broader financial needs. He said Bybit's role is to connect these services securely and efficiently, with regulatory requirements and local accountability embedded in the systems that deliver them. He also said confidence in the crypto market is growing as it develops over the long term, with liquidity remaining important to its progress.

The announcement includes a disclaimer that Bybit is not licensed by the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission and that its services are not available to the public in Hong Kong. It describes Bybit as a platform bringing together investing, trading, payments and wealth-building in a single ecosystem. The company says it combines AI-powered technology, deep global liquidity, robust security and transparent operations. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the positions Zhou set out at the event.

Articles.Title: Bybit CEO Ben Zhou: AI, Tokenization and Connected Infrastructure to Reshape the Future of Finance - TradingView

stories.Headline: Department of Justice forms AI task force
stories.Summary:
The Department of Justice announced on Thursday, November 5, 2026, that it has formed an artificial intelligence task force to protect the department against malicious AI actors. The new group, called the Super Intelligence Task Force or DOJ-SITF, will be co-chaired by Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward and Associate Deputy Attorney General Stephen Weiss. Attorney General Todd Blanche set it up in an October 13 memo. The task force aims to keep American leadership in super intelligence from being undermined by foreign state actors, transnational criminal groups, and individuals or companies committing fraud.

The task force will absorb the work of the AI Litigation Task Force that the department created in January under former Attorney General Pam Bondi, and it will coordinate the department's affirmative civil litigation involving AI. It will also organize criminal and civil enforcement efforts involving AI, recommend enforcement priorities, and develop guidance on prosecuting unlawful AI-related conduct. Blanche said the group will act as the department's main point of contact with the Super Intelligence Force that President Donald Trump announced last month. That separate force is led by National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton and coordinates government engagement with AI companies and other organizations. The move follows a late-September executive order in which Trump told agencies to refer to artificial intelligence as "super intelligence," which he called more accurate.

Blanche said in a statement that the task force will help the department work with Clayton so that critical super intelligence technologies serve the American people and are not manipulated by bad actors at home or abroad. He also said the department will keep identifying and prosecuting people whose use of super intelligence breaks the law, including those who target American taxpayers, critical U.S. infrastructure, or other national security interests. The article notes that the term super intelligence already had an established meaning, which philosopher Nick Bostrom defined as any intellect that greatly exceeds human cognitive performance in virtually all domains, and that this meaning differs from artificial intelligence. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Department of Justice forms AI task force - Nextgov/FCW

stories.Headline: “AI is changing data centre requirements”: Interview with Digital Connexion’s Vikram K.
stories.Summary:
Vikram K., Chief Revenue Officer of Digital Connexion, gave an interview to tele.net in which he said AI is changing data centre requirements. He said India's installed data centre capacity grew from about 375 MW in 2020 to around 1,575 MW in August 2026, citing the Ministry of Electronics and IT. He said the next phase of growth will be shaped by NeoCloud providers, GPU-as-a-service platforms and hyperscalers. He also said Digital Connexion's MAA10 facility in Ambattur, Chennai, received NVIDIA DGX-Ready Data Centre Certification.

The interview gives several figures. MeitY's Rs 103.72 billion outlay is meant to strengthen India's AI ecosystem and widen access to computing for start-ups, researchers and enterprises. India's GPUaaS market earned $284 million in 2025 and is projected to reach $1.2 billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 19.6 per cent between 2026 and 2033. MAA10's magnetic levitation-based air-cooled chillers can deliver up to 15 per cent energy savings, and the facility has the Indian Green Building Council's Green Data Centre Platinum certification.

Vikram said GPU availability alone is not enough, because NeoCloud operators also need high rack densities, substantial power, advanced cooling and robust network connectivity. He said power supply, electrical distribution and thermal management must work as one integrated system. He said Digital Connexion is developing AI-ready infrastructure with a 230 kV substation and a design aimed at a power usage effectiveness of 1.4. He said the company is adopting closed loop liquid cooling, which recirculates water, alongside a water treatment plant.

Vikram said India's potential as a global AI infrastructure hub depends on power availability, grid expansion, supply chain constraints and long-lead equipment. He said early coordination on grid connectivity, power availability and commissioning schedules is important. He cited JLL on the importance of power approvals for new capacity and the International Energy Agency on aligning electricity supply with rising data centre demand. He said the coming phase will be defined by the industry's ability to expand capacity while meeting power, cooling and sustainability needs.

Articles.Title: “AI is changing data centre requirements”: Interview with Digital Connexion’s Vikram K. - tele.net

stories.Headline: GitLab Bets Context, Not Bigger Models, Will Fix AI Agent Costs
stories.Summary:
GitLab made GitLab Orbit generally available on Oct. 29 for Premium and Ultimate customers, and it is live on GitLab.com now. Self-Managed and GitLab Dedicated will follow in the coming weeks. Orbit is a context graph for the software lifecycle that connects code, merge requests, work items, pipelines, vulnerabilities, and ownership in one view that updates as teams ship. Agents query the graph instead of rebuilding the picture themselves.

GitLab says that in its own testing, agents connected to Orbit produced up to 45x fewer hallucinations and used up to 4.5x fewer tokens on the same tasks with the same model. Compare the Market tested four context approaches for an AI code reviewer on 79 real merge requests, and the Orbit-grounded reviewer matched about 70% of expected inline comments while a retrieval-augmented generation approach matched about 58%. Orbit indexes GitLab data and default-branch code into a property graph stored in ClickHouse and runs as a separate service beside GitLab. Results follow existing GitLab permissions, and third-party agents including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode connect through the Model Context Protocol or the GitLab CLI. GitLab sells Orbit in query packs that form one shared pool for the whole organization, at $30 per user per month in GitLab Credits for 1,000 queries, with usage beyond the pool at about $0.03 per query and a 30-day free trial available through GitLab account teams.

Manav Khurana, chief product and marketing officer at GitLab, said AI agents are only as accurate and efficient as the context they work from. Ryan Harvey, head of AI engineering at Compare the Market, said the gap was clear in better comment placement and better summaries of what actually changed, and that RAG, which they had assumed would be the natural solution, ended up performing worse than no context at all. Mitch Ashley, vice president and practice lead at The Futurum Group, said context is becoming surface for effective AI agent behavior and that whoever tells an agent what a change touches, who owns the code, and what broke last week shapes what that agent does next. Ashley also said coverage is the test, since many enterprises run code on more than one platform, and that context stopping at GitLab's edge leaves agents guessing about the rest.

GitLab says more than 3,500 organizations have used Orbit since the beta, running more than 280,000 agent queries. The article notes that Orbit draws on data GitLab already holds and that GitLab says it can extend to other sources. It also notes that the benchmark figures are GitLab's own and that teams should track token use and retry rates in their own environment before and after turning it on. The article says the bigger shift is in how the industry thinks about agent performance, since cost and accuracy depend just as much on what an agent knows when it starts.

Articles.Title: GitLab Bets Context, Not Bigger Models, Will Fix AI Agent Costs - DevOps.com

stories.Headline: Commentary: Reject the Sand God. Call AI by its true name
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to replace the term "artificial intelligence" with "Super Intelligence," arguing that the word "artificial" makes the technology sound fake. The article, an opinion piece by Nico Zviovich of The Alliance for Secure AI, was published by The Derrick on November 5, 2026, and it opposes that change. The author notes that many Americans already treat AI as a trusted advisor, with one-third of teenagers in a Common Sense Media survey saying they had discussed serious personal matters with an AI instead of a person. The Bible Chat app has also been downloaded more than 30 million times, according to the piece.

The new name, the author argues, gives the technology an almost holy status it does not deserve. The author says the rebrand encourages people to see AI as more than a tool, lending it a degree of esoteric knowledge and near-omniscience that the article suggests surpasses human judgment. Faith leaders involved in the author's coalition, which launched in June with more than 60 leaders from different denominations, worry less about a robot uprising than about people taking their problems to chatbots instead of to pastors and other people. The article also points to the "uncanny valley" discomfort people feel around machines that seem almost human, arguing that the word "artificial" helped people keep their guard up.

Trump's order directs agencies to stop using the old terms, but the author notes that reporters and executives, including Elon Musk, keep using the original name anyway. The author draws on the views of Joe Allen, a writer on transhumanism, who argues that the movement to merge humans with machines works like a religion aiming to build "Sand Gods" from silicon made from sand. The author also cites Texas A&M professor Heidi Campbell, who warns that chatbots tell users what they want to hear and that companies store user conversations, unlike a priest bound to keep a confession. Pastor Michael Grayston of LifeFamily Church in Austin, Texas, is quoted saying that AI cannot pray over your children.

Drexel University researchers found that teens' use of AI companions often began as emotional support and turned into dependency resembling addiction. The article also cites a Barna survey finding that 24 percent of pastors use AI to help write or edit sermons. The author recommends that parents know which AI apps their children use, that pastors address AI from the pulpit and be open about their own use, and that everyone keep calling the technology artificial intelligence while bringing personal problems to people instead. The piece makes these arguments as opinion, and the article does not describe any formal action beyond the executive order and the coalition's work.

Articles.Title: Commentary: Reject the Sand God. Call AI by its true name - The Derrick

stories.Headline: Does AI training infringe copyright? CJEU Opinion - Kancelaria Prawna Skarbiec
stories.Summary:
The Court of Justice of the European Union has received its first case about generative AI, and on 3 November 2026 Advocate General Maciej Szpunar delivered his Opinion in Case C-250/25, Like Company v Google Ireland. The dispute began in 2023, when a Hungarian news portal, owned by Like Company Kft., published a short article about a plan to bring freshwater dolphins to an aquarium on Lake Balaton. Later, a user asked Google's chatbot, then called Bard, to summarise that article in Hungarian, and the answer added details the article did not contain. The company sued Google Ireland before a Budapest court, claiming that between 13 June 2023 and 31 May 2024 Google had infringed its rights as a press publisher, and the Hungarian court referred four questions to Luxembourg. The Advocate General's view splits the case in two.

In his reading, training a language model on freely accessible press articles falls in principle within the text and data mining exception in Directive 2019/790, and the press publishers' right does not cover training at all, because training is not online use in the sense the Directive requires. A chatbot that retrieves an article in real time and serves its contents so fully that readers no longer need to visit the publisher's site may, however, infringe that right, and the service provider may be liable where the effect is built into its business model or follows from the absence of safeguards. The Opinion runs to 240 points, and the Advocate General warns that some of his views are provisional. A judgment is expected in 2027, and although the Court is not bound by the Opinion, it usually follows it. The press publishers' right was designed in 2019 with aggregators and media monitoring services in mind.

Article 15 of the Directive gives publishers reproduction and making-available rights over their press publications, but only for online use by information society service providers, and it excludes hyperlinking, individual words and very short extracts, and mere facts. The right expires two years after the year of publication. In Poland it has applied since 20 September 2024 under the Act of 26 July 2024, which amended the Copyright and Related Rights Act, and it entitles the journalists who authored the works to half of the publisher's remuneration. Disputes over the amount go first to mediation before the President of the Office of Electronic Communications, who may issue a binding determination if mediation fails. The Advocate General also treats the protected subject matter as the form of an article, meaning how it is arranged and phrased, and not the underlying news.

The Advocate General says that the second and third questions, which concern training, are hypothetical and should be declared inadmissible, but he discusses them at length anyway. He concludes that training involves reproductions, since copies made during training fall within Article 2 of Directive 2001/29, and he rejects comparing a model to a human learning from reading. He holds that a trained model is not itself a database, so it does not store copies of the works, and he treats memorised fragments as a flaw to be assessed case by case rather than proof of copies inside the model.
