stories.Headline: Acm Research earnings on deck amid advanced packaging push
stories.Summary:
Acm Research is due to report third-quarter results before the market opens on Thursday, November 5, 2026. Analysts expect earnings of 49 cents a share on revenue of $308.5 million, which would be year-over-year growth of 35% and 15%. That earnings figure is down from the $0.61 reported in the second quarter, even though revenue is projected to rise about 5% from the prior period. Earnings estimates have risen 7.81% over the past 60 days, while revenue estimates have stayed largely flat over the past week.

The company recently shipped its first 310×310mm panel-level electroplating production tool, aimed at the AI semiconductor packaging market. It appointed Yue Ma, an ASML veteran, as Chief Operations Officer effective October 1. In August, Acm reported second-quarter earnings of $0.61 per share against a $0.42 consensus, and revenue of $292.9 million, beating estimates by nearly 9%. The stock trades at $45.33, below its 52-week high of $127, with a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 20.6. Nine of ten analysts rate it a buy, with a mean price target of $115.33.

Investors are watching whether Acm can keep its gross margin while ramping advanced packaging equipment, and management comments on customer adoption and packaging revenue will matter. They will also look at operating leverage and supply chain optimization for signs about the expected sequential margin compression. Geographic diversification is another focus, given significant operations in China and the goal of winning share at global foundries. The article does not quote company officials directly.

Separately, Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong visited the company’s Advanced Package Lab in Yokohama, Japan, on November 1, his first on-site inspection since the facility opened. He discussed packaging development progress and possible cooperation with Japanese partners alongside Hiroichi Kawahira, head of Samsung’s DS Research Japan, and Takashi Kariya, head of the lab. Samsung opened the lab on September 8 and set up a local entity in 2023, with plans to invest 40 billion yen over five years starting in 2024. The lab works with Samsung’s packaging research organization in South Korea and covers areas from wafer bonding to glass substrates. Samsung said it will use Yokohama’s talent pool and research infrastructure and develop the lab into a research collaboration hub.

Articles.Title: Acm Research earnings on deck amid advanced packaging push - Investing.com

stories.Headline: KLAC Q1 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and 2027 Growth Outlook
stories.Summary:
KLA Corporation reported results for its first quarter of fiscal 2027 on its earnings call, with revenues of $4.14 billion beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.05 billion, and adjusted earnings of $1.22 per share topping the consensus estimate of $1.18. CEO Rick Wallace pointed to accelerating investments in leading-edge foundry and logic manufacturing, high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging as the main demand drivers. CFO Bren Higgins raised KLA's calendar 2026 wafer fabrication equipment market expectation to the mid-$150 billion range, including advanced packaging, and management expects the market to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027. The company reported a 62.7% non-GAAP gross margin and a record operating margin of 46.1% in the September quarter.

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, KLA expects revenues of $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million, and non-GAAP earnings of $1.44 per share, plus or minus 11 cents. Higgins expects December-quarter operating expenses of approximately $710 million. Wallace said advanced packaging process control systems revenue remains on track to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, representing more than 70% year-over-year growth, which is nearly twice the expected growth rate of the advanced packaging market. Management expects advanced packaging to keep outgrowing its underlying market in 2027, and it expects greater investment in 2-nanometer and emerging 1.4-nanometer logic technologies during 2027.

Higgins said elevated memory component costs remain a profitability headwind, and he discussed product cost reductions, memory optimization and pricing initiatives, expecting improvement toward the company's 63% to 64% gross margin target in the latter part of 2027 and into 2028. He said equipment lead times average approximately 12 months, with certain advanced systems requiring longer, and that KLA continues expanding manufacturing capacity and coordinating investments with critical suppliers. Wallace emphasized maintaining technological leadership and supporting customer manufacturing roadmaps, and executives acknowledged that customer facility readiness and infrastructure constraints can influence equipment delivery schedules. Higgins projected sequential revenue growth over the next several quarters, supported by expanding backlog and improving customer visibility, with a more consistent growth trajectory throughout 2027.

The articles note that KLA faces competition in advanced packaging, with Onto Innovation raising its 2026 advanced packaging growth outlook to approximately 80% from 50% and Applied Materials expecting its packaging revenues to grow more than 70% in 2026. KLA shares have risen 37.8% year to date compared with 17.4% growth for the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, and the stock trades at a forward 12-month price/earnings of 28.68X versus 19.39X for the sector. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for KLA's fiscal 2027 earnings is $5.44 per share, up 2 cents over the past 30 days and suggesting 44.7% growth. KLA currently has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) in one article and a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) in the other, and the articles say the company will need to manage supply constraints and increase production capacity to meet customer requirements.

stories.Headline: AI Demand Burns Through 2029 as Cathay Forum Flags HBM, Advanced Packaging and Taiwan-Korea Complementary Opportunities
stories.Summary:
Cathay Securities Investment Trust and Daiwa-Cathay Capital Markets held an AI investment forum on the 4th during Taiwan Week. The event, titled From Silicon Valley to Silicon Island: The Investment Map in the AI Era, brought together experts from Japan's Daiwa Securities, the South Korean technology industry and Cathay's research team. It opened with remarks from Cathay Chief Investment Officer Cheng Li-cheng, Daiwa Managing Executive Officer Naoki Suzuki and Daiwa-Cathay President Takeshi Mitsuda. Presentations followed from Daiwa's South Korean technology expert Sung Kyu Kim, Cathay's Taiwan-Korea technology expert Li Han-lin, Taiwan equity semiconductor expert Huang Chiu-wen and fund manager Liang En-yi.

Sung Kyu Kim said AI applications are spreading from model training to inference, agentic AI and physical AI, making memory a key link that affects overall performance. He said demand for HBM capacity and bandwidth is climbing as AI chip specifications rise, and that future AI agents will need longer context and more complex tasks, boosting DRAM and NAND demand. He cited industry expectations that Samsung sees memory supply tightness persisting through 2028, while SK Hynix's visibility on DRAM and HBM demand extends to 2029. He said Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Google, the four major cloud service providers, continue to ramp up AI capital expenditure as the main driver of the memory upcycle.

Li Han-lin said chip process miniaturization is nearing physical limits, Moore's Law is slowing and DRAM process upgrades have become markedly more difficult. He said growing complexity in HBM and high-layer NAND stacking raises the capital, equipment and time needed for capacity expansion, so tight memory supply and demand may persist. He said South Korea leads in memory such as DRAM and HBM, while Taiwan controls advanced process technology, advanced packaging and the AI server supply chain. He described the two industries as highly complementary and together an indispensable part of global AI infrastructure.

Huang Chiu-wen said AI demand has expanded from GPUs to CPUs, memory, communications and power systems, driving upgrades across Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain. He said Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing continues to expand CoWoS capacity, which is expected to drive demand for packaging and testing equipment, IC substrates, facility engineering and semiconductor materials. He said optical communications and co-packaged optics are drawing attention as transmission speeds move toward 800G and 1.6T, and power architecture is moving toward high-voltage direct current. He cautioned that not all suppliers will benefit equally and that it remains to be seen whether specification upgrades raise unit prices and added value.

Liang En-yi said the long-term AI growth trend remains intact but beneficiary companies are not fixed, so allocation needs to adjust as demand extends to advanced packaging, optical communications and power management. He described a one offense, one defense strategy in which the Cathay Active Momentum High Dividend Fund (00400A) screens roughly 40 to 60 stocks from more than 1,900 listed and OTC companies. He said the Cathay Taiwan High Dividend Fund focuses on earnings quality, dividend records and valuation reasonableness. Cathay said investors can participate through the Cathay Taiwan-Korea Technology ETF (00735) or other allocations based on their own objectives and risk tolerance, while remaining mindful of risks such as semiconductor cyclicality, industry concentration and market volatility.

Articles.Title: AI Demand Burns Through 2029 as Cathay Forum Flags HBM, Advanced Packaging and Taiwan-Korea Complementary Opportunities - BigGo Finance

stories.Headline: MediaTek Recruits Former Intel Executive Vice President Shahriari to Lead Advanced Packaging, Deepen TSMC Collaboration
stories.Summary:
MediaTek announced on November 4, 2026, that it has recruited former Intel Executive Vice President Navid Shahriari as Senior Vice President, effective November 9, reporting to President and Chief Operating Officer Joe Chen. Shahriari brings 37 years of experience in semiconductor design engineering and advanced packaging, and he retired from Intel in June this year after serving as Executive Vice President of Intel Foundry. At Intel he was mainly responsible for back-end process operations, covering packaging, testing and advanced packaging strategy, and he drove the company's chiplet integration and testing technology efforts. This is MediaTek's second major hire in advanced packaging, after former TSMC R&D Vice President Yu Chen-hua joined as an advisor in May this year.

In the role, Shahriari will lead teams responsible for the advanced process and yield platform, design technology co-optimization, advanced testing and packaging, and quality and reliability. MediaTek said one of his core missions is to deepen collaboration with key supply chain partners including Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, so that close coordination and integration of advanced technologies can help MediaTek keep launching competitive artificial intelligence and high-performance computing products. MediaTek named TSMC specifically in its press release, tying the mission to the company's future development strategy. The company said Shahriari also has hands-on experience in the data center market.

MediaTek said the appointment supports its push into data center and AI investments, and industry observers said the successive hires from TSMC and Intel show its commitment to the data center business now extends from product planning to manufacturing and packaging execution. Institutional investors are watching whether MediaTek can build its own coordination capabilities in advanced packaging, reduce dependence on external resources, and secure more favorable process and capacity arrangements in its work with TSMC. The arrival of senior packaging talent is seen as one of the supporting conditions for MediaTek to win orders from cloud service providers, since AI ASIC projects often involve long-term customer procurement commitments. Advanced packaging capacity remains a bottleneck across the AI supply chain, and whether MediaTek turns the talent advantage into actual project progress will depend on coordination with foundry and packaging and testing partners.

Articles.Title: MediaTek Recruits Former Intel Executive Vice President Shahriari to Lead Advanced Packaging, Deepen TSMC Collaboration - BigGo Finance

stories.Headline: Qualcomm HBC Compared to HBM
stories.Summary:
Qualcomm announced on November 2, 2026, that it has validated first-generation silicon for its high-bandwidth computing (HBC) architecture in the lab. The company said its engineers used industry-standard automated test equipment to confirm the complete memory read-write path and near-memory computations at production levels. Qualcomm first introduced the HBC architecture in July 2026 as a way to address the memory wall in AI inference. The validation comes ahead of sampling for the Dragonfly AI250, which Qualcomm says is due for release next year.

The testing found that HBC can deliver as much as 18 times the memory bandwidth of LPDDR and an energy-efficiency measurement of five times the terabit-per-second-per-watt compared to HBM4, the sixth generation of high-bandwidth memory. In HBC, a stack of LPDDR-based memory sits in the package with a compute die underneath it, so data moves across micrometers rather than millimeters. Qualcomm says this gives the AI model faster access to data and reduces the time, energy and cost of moving it. The AI250 is expected to start sampling in the first half of 2027, with Dragonfly C1000 CPUs also set for next year and Dragonfly AI300 samples coming in 2028.

Gerardo Giaretta, vice president and general manager of datacenter CPU and AI at Qualcomm, said traditional architectures have plenty of DDR capacity but a narrow link that moves data slowly, while HBM increases lanes and speed at a premium in cost, power and complex packaging. He described HBC as a co-processor where most decode operations happen inside the package, so the slower link to the AI250 does not affect end-to-end performance because only results are sent back. He said the solution gives the bandwidth needed at the lowest energy, with at least an order of magnitude less energy spent moving data. He also said the validation is important because HBC is a clear differentiator, since the compute sits under the memory stack, and that it should erase doubts about high-yield manufacturing of the AI250 next year.

Qualcomm has for more than a year been working to become a larger player in the AI datacenter space and an alternative to Nvidia. HBC will be integrated into the Dragonfly AI250 to create what executives call a full AI inference accelerator platform, which will be foundational to the Qualcomm Dragonfly Rack for inference workloads. Giaretta said Qualcomm is working with various partners on different ways HBC can be used and that the AI250 is not the only product where it will appear. He said the company usually does not do a blog or pre-briefing for a chip bring-up, but did so because the technology is completely new.

stories.Headline: Shares of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell more than 40 to 50% from their high points, but the
stories.Summary:
On November 5, 2026, shares of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell sharply, with Samsung trading at 205,500 won, down 12,500 won, and SK Hynix at 1,295,000 won, down 101,000 won, according to the Korea Exchange. Both stocks were down about 45 percent from their June peaks, Samsung from 374,500 won and SK Hynix by a nearly identical amount. The wider KOSPI fell 4.17 percent to 5,446.79 as of 10:39 a.m., after opening down 1.82 percent and dropping as low as 5,386.29, and the index stood 41.97 percent below its all-time high of 9,385.59 set on June 19. The Korea Exchange triggered a sell sidecar at 10:16 a.m., its 56th KOSPI activation this year and 29th in the sell direction, which suspends program sell orders for five minutes when KOSPI 200 futures stay down more than 5 percent for one minute.

The trigger was the U.S. midterm elections held on the 3rd, where the Democratic Party won majorities in both the Senate and the House. Democratic wins in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, key data center regions, raised concerns about restrictions on new data center permits and delays in semiconductor orders. Foreign investors net sold 1 trillion 125.2 billion won and institutions 6 billion won on KOSPI, while retail investors net bought 1 trillion 46.2 billion won. In the U.S., the Dow rose 3.03 percent to 53,356.12 and the NASDAQ 1.44 percent to 25,736.51, but the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.13 percent. On KOSDAQ, down 4.30 percent to 684.19, foreigners net sold 136.9 billion won.

KB Securities forecast combined operating profit for the two companies of 1,110.5 trillion won, the first time above 1,000 trillion won, with researcher Kim Dong-won projecting fourth-quarter operating profit of 128 trillion won for Samsung and 104 trillion won for SK Hynix, up 539 percent and 441 percent from a year earlier. iM Securities issued a buy rating and 2.3 million won target for SK Hynix on the 4th, expecting operating profit of 45.3 trillion won next year and 54.2 trillion won in 2028, with HBM sales rising from 43 trillion won this year to 183 trillion won in 2028. Researcher Ko Eui-young said the higher the HBM share, the lower the volatility of the company's profit, and that SK Hynix is at the forefront of the industry. Researcher Yang Hyeon-kyung of iM Securities said expectations for reduced cost burdens from falling oil prices are spreading to aviation and transportation, and that it is necessary to check whether rotation trading will appear in non-semiconductor sectors. Researcher Byun Jun-ho of IBK Investment & Securities said markets after midterm elections have tended to react more sensitively to positive news, and that the KOSPI recently plunged to around 1 times its 12-month forward price-to-book ratio, indicating extreme undervaluation.

KB Securities expects HBM's share of global DRAM production capacity to expand from 18 percent in 2025 to 30 percent next year, while general-purpose DRAM falls from 82 percent to 70 percent, and expects Samsung to secure 70 percent of total production capacity through long-term supply contracts by 2030. iM Securities noted SK Hynix fell 57 percent from its June high to its October low, more than the average 51 percent fall in past semiconductor downturns, and that the adjustment took about 4 months rather than the past 8 to 13 months. It predicted SK Hynix's return on equity will remain highly profitable at 47 percent in 2028. Analysts said investors should weigh memory demand from AI investment, HBM competitive advantage and the sustainability of supply shortages rather than treat the fall as a buying opportunity, and warned that a slowdown in big tech AI investment or full-scale expansion by memory companies could dampen HBM demand and memory prices.
