stories.Headline: KOTRA Partners With Data Center Group to Draw Foreign AI Investment
stories.Summary:
KOTRA signed a memorandum of understanding with the Korea Data Center Council on Nov. 4 at the Parnas Hotel in Seoul to expand foreign investment in artificial intelligence data centers. KOTRA announced the agreement on the 5th. The deal combines KOTRA's overseas network with the council's industry expertise to identify foreign investment demand. Kim Tae-hyung, head of Invest Korea at KOTRA, Lee Han-cheol, investment policy director at the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, and Kang Joong-hyup, chairman of the Korea Data Center Council, posed for a photo after the signing.

The cooperation covers finding and promoting foreign investment demand for data centers, publishing a guide to building data centers, supporting cooperation between foreign investors and domestic data center companies, and resolving investment obstacles. JPMorgan projects that $5.5 trillion will be invested in global AI data center infrastructure by 2030. The Korean government has designated data centers, along with semiconductors and physical AI, as one of three mega projects. Under the plan, the private sector will lead with 550 trillion won to build 8.4 gigawatts of AI data center capacity, while the government provides support and fosters industry ecosystems.

A special act on promoting the data center industry takes effect in March next year, covering one-stop permit processing and special provisions for power supply outside the greater Seoul area. The two sides held a meeting with foreign-invested data center companies on Oct. 23 to hear about difficulties in securing electricity and obtaining permits and to determine what support they need. Based on those views, KOTRA and the council plan to publish a guidebook on the procedures and rules foreign investors need to know, timed to the law's implementation. They also agreed to work together to resolve obstacles that arise during the investment process.

Articles.Title: KOTRA Partners With Data Center Group to Draw Foreign AI Investment - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: LG Turns to AI for Plant Safety, Halting Equipment on Risk Alerts
stories.Summary:
LG Corp. is putting artificial intelligence at the center of how it manages workplace safety. AI systems analyze closed-circuit television footage to detect hazards and automatically shut down equipment, and they also review the complex safety documentation required at chemical plants. The group has also developed an AI app that identifies risks at subcontractors' work sites. LG said on the 5th that it held its group-wide safety, health and environment conference, LG SHEC, over two days starting on the 4th at LG Science Park in Seoul's Magok district. The event, launched in 2023 and now in its fourth year, drew about 350 safety and environment officials from 16 affiliates, including LG Electronics, LG Chem and LG Display.

Twenty officials from overseas operations in the U.S., China and India also attended. This year's theme was "Drive the Shift," reflecting a push to overhaul safety management in step with advances in AI and robotics. Of the 21 innovation cases presented at the event, 15 involved AI. LG Electronics presented an integrated control system that uses AI to analyze footage from 4,226 CCTV cameras installed at its domestic plants and construction sites. When the AI detects a hazard, it halts equipment or blocks access.

LG Chem has introduced AI into process safety management, the work of preventing fires and explosions at chemical plants. An in-house AI agent cross-checks documents across nine areas, including equipment modifications and inspections, to verify compliance with safety procedures, and the system has cut document review time by 98%. LG Display developed a system that uses AI to analyze workers' postures and assess the risk of musculoskeletal disorders. It measures strain on the lower back and shoulders and proposes improvements, and assessments that previously took 30 minutes now take six. LG Uplus built an AI app that identifies risk factors and preventive measures once a telecom construction subcontractor enters details about a job, and it also drafts materials for pre-work safety briefings automatically.

Since the app was adopted, risk assessment standards at 21 subcontractors have improved 27% from previous levels. The conference also featured expert lectures on AI and robotics technology and on industrial safety policy, and LG named six sites as model workplaces for their accident prevention and safety management records and gave them awards. An LG official said advances in AI technology are an opportunity to raise the standard of safety and environmental management. The official said LG will spread these innovation cases to each of its sites and build an environment where everyone can work with peace of mind.

Articles.Title: LG Turns to AI for Plant Safety, Halting Equipment on Risk Alerts - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: New AI data center coming to Glencoe. Here’s what residents and city leaders are saying
stories.Summary:
A new artificial intelligence data center is under construction in Glencoe, with city leaders calling it an economic opportunity while some residents question its effect on the community. The facility is being built at 670 11th St. W. on the city's western edge by Revolve Labs, which already operated a small cryptocurrency mining operation in Glencoe. According to the company, the project covers about 6.25 acres and nearly 94,100 square feet across three buildings. The company says the site will handle AI inference, the computing that runs when artificial intelligence systems generate responses. Construction is already underway, and city leaders say council members approved the development agreement in late August or early September.

Under its agreement with the city, the facility is limited to 200,000 gallons of water per day, while Glencoe's water treatment system has a capacity of about 1.8 million gallons per day. City Administrator Mark Lemen said the city can shut off the water if the facility goes above that limit. Revolve Labs' materials say an independent acoustical consultant projected sound levels of 44 decibels at the nearest residential area, below Minnesota's nighttime residential limit of 50 decibels, and that more testing will follow the opening. The company estimates the project will create 20 to 30 technical jobs and 9 to 10 security jobs, and could generate $500,000 to $600,000 a year in property taxes shared by the city, county and school district. Lemen said Revolve Labs is not seeking tax abatement, tax increment financing or any other subsidy.

Company materials once listed a target completion date of April 2027, but Lemen said the facility is now tentatively expected to be operational by late May or early June. Lemen said the discussions began roughly 18 months ago and took place in open public meetings, with no closed-door conversations. He said city officials spent months checking whether local infrastructure could support the project and wrote safeguards into the development agreement to protect residents. Mayor Mark Hueser said the site sits in an industrial area with no buildings close by, and he noted it is much smaller than some large data center proposals elsewhere in Minnesota. One resident, who asked not to be identified, said residents should have been allowed to vote and worried about higher utility bills.

City leaders responded that a public vote is not required for a private business development and that the proposal went through the city's planning, zoning and council approval process. Lemen said the city wants the project to help attract future investment and support growth in Glencoe. Residents' concerns about water, noise and utility costs are part of a wider debate over data centers, and Minnesota already has dozens of them. Revolve Labs' project is due to open in late spring or early summer 2027, with the sound testing and water limit serving as the main checks on its operation. The articles do not say whether any further votes or reviews are planned before the facility opens.

Articles.Title: New AI data center coming to Glencoe. Here’s what residents and city leaders are saying - 5 EYEWITNESS NEWS

stories.Headline: '30 Days of Work in One': Public Servant Builds AI Safety Platform
stories.Summary:
Shin Hae-seop, an administrative officer at the Construction Headquarters of Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City, developed a facility safety management platform himself beginning in January 2026. The project grew out of the difficulties he faced managing hundreds of road facilities such as bridges, tunnels, underpasses and retaining walls, which deteriorate as they age. As the number of facilities kept growing, officials had to check inspection schedules and targets one by one, and legal standards differ by facility type. Staff also had to draw up design specification documents by hand each time a safety inspection contract went out to bid. No outside contractor was hired and no separate budget was allocated, and Shin used artificial intelligence as a development tool.

The platform automatically classifies inspection targets based on the legal standards for each facility type, analyzes whether higher-level inspections have been carried out, and determines whether lower-level inspections can be skipped. Damage, cracks and repair and reinforcement records that had been scattered across individual reports are now consolidated by facility, so users can check whether a crack in the same location is widening or whether a repair is coming due. Work that previously took more than 30 days for safety inspection and diagnostic contracts now takes less than a day. The platform automates data verification, the application of calculation standards and document preparation, which cuts repetitive administrative work and speeds up contract awards.

Records are no longer lost when staff change, according to the article. Son Du-yeong, head of the Construction Headquarters, said administrative innovation using AI and digital technology improves work efficiency and contributes to public safety. He added that the city will continue to upgrade its facility safety management system and expand administrative services that employees and residents can feel in practice. Officials said the system is highly usable because it was created by a public servant who knows the field best, in the language of the field.

Separately, Fraunhofer researchers are developing an AI-driven civil protection dashboard with partners in the RegioGuard-PRO project, which runs from March 2026 through March 2028 and is funded by the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space. The project builds on two earlier projects, AKRIMA and HERAKLION, and a ready-to-use demonstrator is planned within two years. Research scientist Kai Fischer said municipalities often have vast amounts of data during crises but it is scattered across sources and not interconnected, and that the platform consolidates and analyzes large data sets to enable early detection of hazards. Demonstration centers are being established in Trier, Mainz and Wildau to test the dashboard under realistic field conditions, with the aim of eventually deploying it in other regions.

Articles.Title: '30 Days of Work in One': Public Servant Builds AI Safety Platform - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: HSAD Builds AI Agent to Forecast Netflix Ad Reach
stories.Summary:
HSAD said on November 5 that it has built an artificial intelligence agent that can forecast the expected reach of Netflix advertising before campaigns run. The agency combined AI with data held by Netflix to analyze a range of ad placement scenarios. It linked Netflix's official advertising reach forecast application programming interface to DASH, its in-house AI agent platform. The aim is to help advertisers allocate budgets and set strategy.

Advertisers can enter their target audience and budget in everyday language, without complex data analysis, and see projected reach and the scale of impressions. The tool lets them check expected reach when spending on a specific age group, or compare results from directing the same budget at different target audiences. HSAD is also developing an integrated system for forecasting advertising effectiveness across television, PCs, mobile devices and over-the-top streaming services. The plan is to link Netflix ad data to MPOPS, its existing media planning system, and analyze factors such as duplicate reach between media and the added reach gained by including another medium. The company is targeting a launch of the integrated forecasting system within the year.

An HSAD official said that the more complex the media environment becomes, the more important it is to accurately predict the overall effect created by a combination of media, beyond the performance of individual channels. The official said the company will raise the sophistication of its media strategy through detailed, data-driven analysis and forecasting. The report was written by Kim Kyung-taek for Seoul Economic Daily and translated from Korean by AI. The article says quotes from foreign sources are based on Korean-language reports and may not reflect exact original wording.

Articles.Title: HSAD Builds AI Agent to Forecast Netflix Ad Reach - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Vision AI Becomes the Store Clerk That Watches, Sells and Restocks
stories.Summary:
Vision artificial intelligence is being used in South Korean retail stores to watch shoppers, target advertising and speed up checkout. GS Retail runs vision AI at about 300 GS25 and GS The Fresh stores, where cameras beside digital displays record visitors and measure how long they look at ads. The system sorts visitors by age group and gender, and the company compares that data with product sales to judge advertising effectiveness. Shinsegae I&C installed a smart checkout counter called Sparos Scan Free in May last year at employee cafeterias at SK hynix campuses in Icheon and Cheongju. The startup Deeping Source released software called Sci-Care last year that flags problems in CCTV footage, such as shelves that have not been restocked or refrigerator doors left open.

Sparos Scan Free lets shoppers check out without scanning barcodes, because a camera captures the items on the counter and the AI identifies each product and calculates the total price. The company says it identifies items with 99.9% accuracy even when several products sit together or overlap and are partly hidden. Shinsegae I&C is in talks with food and beverage brands to supply the system. Sci-Care classifies situations by type of incident and sends alerts to staff based on preset operating standards. It has been adopted at some 7-Eleven stores in South Korea and is currently installed at some 150 stores at home and abroad, and companies in Japan and Thailand have shown interest.

Lee Jung-pyo, an executive director leading GS Retail's vision AI advertising and marketing business, said companies must build a loop in which the results of data interpretation feed into campaigns and the outcomes are measured again. Kim Jung-eon, head of Shinsegae I&C's AI technology team, said the biggest advantage of Sparos Scan Free is the ease of registering new products, because the system can learn product information immediately from just three photos taken on the counter. Kim Tae-hoon, chief executive of Deeping Source, said sales records do not show how long a customer examined a product or waited in line, and that measuring what happens in a store as data can change how a company runs its business. Lee said adopting vision AI in retail should be approached as a management challenge rather than a simple information technology project.

The articles describe retail as fundamentally about people serving people in a specific space, and say trends, advertising, store interiors and service attitudes all influence what consumers buy but do not show up on a receipt. Retailers are adopting vision AI to capture these previously invisible situations and consumer behaviors and record them as data. Three elements are seen as essential: information collection, data analysis and personal data protection. Companies must continuously gather information and analyze the data they need while protecting customers' personal information to earn trust.

Articles.Title: Vision AI Becomes the Store Clerk That Watches, Sells and Restocks - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Adobe Offers Free AI Tools to Startups Under Five Years Old
stories.Summary:
Adobe has launched a program called Adobe for Startups that gives companies founded within the past five years free access to its artificial intelligence tools for 12 months. The company said the program is meant to help early-stage startups build their brands, produce content and expand customer touchpoints. Adobe announced the program on the 5th, according to a Seoul Economic Daily report dated Nov. 4, 2026. Qualifying startups can use Adobe Firefly Pro Plus, Acrobat Studio including Adobe Express Premium, and Semrush.

Firefly Pro Plus is an all-in-one AI studio for creating image, video and audio content, with access to Adobe's own models, partner models and Photoshop for web and mobile. Acrobat Studio combines PDF tools, an AI assistant and Adobe Express in one solution that supports document editing and sharing, presentation building and signature collection. Express Premium is a content creation app for producing posts and marketing materials for various social media channels, and it comes with professional-grade templates. Startups can also use Semrush to track how customers discover their brands, measuring how brands appear in search results and AI-powered search.

Eligibility is limited to startups founded within the past five years that have raised less than $15 million, and Adobe reviews whether applicants meet the requirements during the application process. Adobe also plans to host a hands-on workshop called Brand on Demand on Dec. 3, where participating companies can learn from Adobe experts and network with other founders. Adobe said the program brings together tools for content creation, document productivity and marketing so startups can move quickly without adding complexity to their work. The company added that startups will be able to tap professional-grade Adobe technology from their earliest days.

Articles.Title: Adobe Offers Free AI Tools to Startups Under Five Years Old - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Toss Securities Adds AI Screening to Block Illegal Stock Tip Rooms
stories.Summary:
Toss Securities introduced an artificial intelligence-based screening system for posts on its investment community platform, the brokerage said on the 4th. The system analyzes a post's title, body text and images together whenever a post is written or edited. It detects profanity, defamation and expressions of hate or discrimination, as well as content that could undermine investor protection, such as promotions for illegal stock tip rooms. Depending on the severity of the violation, posts are either excluded from recommendations or hidden.

The company said the key change is that the review now covers the content and context of an entire post, rather than simply checking whether it contains banned words. The banned-word filter applied at the writing stage has also been strengthened, and it now uses AI to catch altered or disguised versions of banned terms. Instead of blocking an entire post because it contains a banned word, the system now lets users publish the post with the flagged expression masked. Posts therefore go through a two-stage review, with banned words filtered first when a post is written and the AI checking the content again after it is published.

Toss Securities also overhauled its community rules and drew up content guidelines for the service. The guidelines set out restrictions on profanity, harmful content, hate and discriminatory expressions, promotional material and advertising, and conduct that disrupts market order. When a post is hidden, the company explains the reason for the action and offers an appeals process. An official at Toss Securities said the company focused on reducing cases where users are exposed to inappropriate investment solicitations or offensive posts, and that it will continue to improve the community environment so that investors can share useful information and exchange a range of views.

Articles.Title: Toss Securities Adds AI Screening to Block Illegal Stock Tip Rooms - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: U.S. Power Line Construction Falls 77% in Decade, Choking AI Buildout
stories.Summary:
U.S. high-voltage transmission line construction fell sharply over the past decade, according to a Financial Times report cited by Seoul Economic Daily on November 3. About 6,400 kilometers of lines were built in 2013, but the figure dropped to less than 1,450 kilometers in 2024. Major transmission lines now take an average of 10 years to build, twice as long as it took to construct the Hoover Dam in the 1930s. The Cardinal-Hickory Creek line, a 164-kilometer project carrying wind power from Iowa to Middleton, Wisconsin, took 13 years to complete after local approval in 2011 and ran 40 percent over its original budget.

The slowdown is expected to complicate U.S. AI ambitions, because data centers need transmission networks to carry electricity to where it is required. Consulting firm Grid Strategies projects that power demand will rise by 166 gigawatts by 2030, the equivalent of adding 15 New York Cities. Most of the U.S. grid was built during the construction boom of the 1960s and 1970s and is now nearing the end of its service life. By contrast, China has built more transmission lines over the past 15 years than the U.S. has built in its entire history.

Krista Tanner, chief executive of ITC, which led construction of the Cardinal-Hickory Creek line, said the key question for AI and advanced manufacturing is whether the infrastructure to build it is in place, and she is increasingly worried the answer is no. Ari Peskoe, director of the Electricity Law Initiative at Harvard Law School, said the country has supplied power to growth industries for more than a century, and if it can no longer do so it will lose its economic vitality. Chaz Teplin of the think tank RMI said the actual boundaries of the grid do not line up with political boundaries and are intermingled, and he asked who then holds decision-making power. Advait Arun of the Center for Public Enterprise said regulators can mandate deliberation over which lines should be built, but the structure leaves no one able to compel construction.

Authority in the U.S. system is divided among utilities, private generators, regional grid operators, state regulators and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, and no single body can plan and execute large-scale projects spanning multiple regions. Utilities often oppose long-distance lines that would open their service territories to cheaper power from other regions, and the seven regional grid operators rarely plan large interregional projects together. Of 18 related lawsuits examined by the Niskanen Center, 16 ended in dismissal or defeat, yet construction was delayed by years as cases piled up. Ben Alling, co-founder of data center developer Monarch Energy, warned that saying power will be available only in 10 years amounts to saying it is effectively impossible.

Articles.Title: U.S. Power Line Construction Falls 77% in Decade, Choking AI Buildout - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: How to use AI and ChatGPT to avoid falling victim to fraud or scams - ABC7 New York
stories.Summary:
A consumer segment on ABC7 New York, reported by Nina Pineda and published on November 6, 2026, describes a new way people are using artificial intelligence to protect themselves from scams. The report says that as AI grows more capable, scams are becoming more complex, and it cites Federal Trade Commission data showing 55,000 fraud reports from New York this year alone. The FTC figures also show consumers have lost more than $330 million this year, with a median loss of $305 per person. The segment frames the trend as fighting fire with fire, meaning people are turning to AI tools to spot the very scams that AI is helping to make more convincing.

The report explains the approach through a framework from OpenAI executives, who describe scams as having a ping, a zing, and a sting. The ping is the first unsolicited contact, such as a cold call or text, the zing is emotional language meant to frighten or excite the target, and the sting is the request for money, a credit card number, or other sensitive information. Jack Stubbs, who leads the intelligence and investigative team at OpenAI, said the company works to disrupt bad actors who try to use ChatGPT for criminal activity. He said millions of people are using ChatGPT to spot scams by sharing a suspicious message with the tool, which can quickly point out risk signals. He also said the tool offers a calm second opinion that is free of the emotional pressure scammers rely on.

To test this advice, the station's 7 On Your Side team pasted a recently received text about part-time work into ChatGPT. The tool judged the message to be a scam and advised against contacting the sender. Stubbs stressed that the goal is to give people the information they need to make their own informed decisions about risky messages. The article's closing advice is that people who are skeptical of AI should instead research suspicious links or emails through Google, Facebook, a local consumer agency, or the Better Business Bureau. It also urges consumers never to give personal or financial information in response to an unsolicited request, which it calls a sure sign of a scam.

Articles.Title: How to use AI and ChatGPT to avoid falling victim to fraud or scams - ABC7 New York

stories.Headline: AI Power Grid Tools Take Center Stage at Korea's BIXPO
stories.Summary:
The Bitgaram International Exposition of Electric Power Technology, known as BIXPO, opened on Nov. 4 at the Kim Dae-jung Convention Center in Gwangju. At the Korea Electric Power Corp. pavilion, a demonstration showed surplus solar power stored during the day and sent to nearby homes and buildings at night. A guide said AI analyzes how much more renewable energy can be connected. The exhibit was an AI-based virtual grid that replicates actual power plants, substations and transmission lines on a computer.

KEPCO plans to validate the technology within this year and begin developing applications for Jeju Special Self-Governing Province and the Honam region from 2027. According to the International Energy Agency, a data center takes one to three years to build, while a new power grid can take five to 15 years. Global data center electricity consumption is projected to nearly double to 950 terawatt-hours in 2030 from 485 terawatt-hours in 2025. The Korea Energy Economics Institute found that a shortage of transmission lines in the greater Seoul area is the key constraint on where data centers can be located in South Korea.

Since last month, the government has run a pilot program in Jinan, Jeonbuk State, and Geumsan, South Chungcheong Province, that adjusts transmission limits to seasonal peak temperatures. According to the U.S. Department of Energy, Texas utility Oncor raised transmission limits by 6% to 14% on lines fitted with dynamic line rating sensors. Iljin Electric said it deployed a 154-kilovolt polypropylene-insulated cable, co-developed with KEPCO, in Eumseong, North Chungcheong Province, and that it can carry more than 10% more power than conventional products. LS Electric and LG Uplus signed an agreement on July 21 to jointly verify 800-volt direct current distribution.

Kim Jung-sang, a professor at Duke University who gave the opening keynote, said electricity use has risen as developers train ever-larger models to reduce AI errors. He said that if the computation for training grows fivefold each year and data and energy use expand at the same rate, the total would be 125 times current levels in three years. He said this trend cannot continue and cited the human brain as a far more efficient learning device. Kim, a co-founder of quantum computing company IonQ, also named quantum computing as another technology that could take on the problem.

Articles.Title: AI Power Grid Tools Take Center Stage at Korea's BIXPO - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Kakao Bets on 50 Million KakaoTalk Users in AI Agent Race
stories.Summary:
Kakao said on November 5, 2026, that it will use the relationship network built by 50 million KakaoTalk users to compete with global big tech firms in the race to develop artificial intelligence agents. The company announced the plan during its third-quarter 2026 earnings conference call. CEO Chung Shina said Kakao plans to offer differentiated AI services based on KakaoTalk, where users' interests and relationship context have accumulated. Kakao also intends to develop a new advertising revenue model that identifies users' purchase intent.

Chung said many recently launched AI agents first integrate with external services such as email, calendars and messengers to better understand users and deliver personalized services. She said a standalone AI app must depend on outside platforms for personalized information, and its experience is limited by what those platforms permit. KakaoTalk, she said, already holds a wide range of information, interests and relationship context tied to users' daily lives. She called the relationship network that 50 million users have built through long periods of conversation a powerful competitive strength unique to Kakao and difficult to secure in a short time.

Chung said KakaoTalk's relationship network could expand beyond communication between people to communication between AI agents. She said communication on KakaoTalk involves making plans with family, friends and colleagues, coordinating schedules and deciding matters together, which aligns with how agents check and coordinate information for their users. She said KakaoTalk will develop into a space where users and agents communicate and agents cooperate with one another to handle tasks. On advertising, she said Kakao will be able to understand user context and intent more accurately and recommend products or services at the right moment, creating new demand similar to search advertising.

Kakao will also use AI to strengthen its existing advertising business. Chung said the company plans to advance its machine learning technology and build, by the first quarter of next year, an infrastructure that lets AI understand user behavior and preferences. In December, Kakao will run a closed beta test of Moment AI Krew, a conversational advertising operations agent that supports ad placement and management. Chung said that from next year, Kakao will show how improved advertising efficiency through AI and new monetization opportunities translate into actual revenue growth.

Articles.Title: Kakao Bets on 50 Million KakaoTalk Users in AI Agent Race - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: PNNL: Two Genesis Awards Support AI-Powered Grid Planning
stories.Summary:
The Department of Energy has awarded Genesis Mission funding to Pacific Northwest National Laboratory for two projects that use artificial intelligence to speed up grid planning. The announcement, dated November 5, 2026, follows growth in electricity demand and changing technology that have pushed grid operators to rethink how they plan for the future. Grid planners rely on large models, and those models can now produce tens of thousands of scenarios, more than human teams can review efficiently. The articles frame the awards as an effort to help the grid handle more demand and more complex swings in load and generation. The first project, led by PNNL's Marcelo Elizondo, targets electromagnetic transient models, which simulate how new loads or generation types affect grid behavior at microsecond resolution.

These models are computationally heavy, so the team will test a machine learning approach that approximates complex calculations, which Elizondo described as a "model of a model." The partners include Argonne National Laboratory, Sandia National Laboratories, Siemens Corporation, Washington State University, Xcel Energy Services, and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas. The second project, led by Arizona State University with PNNL as a partner, addresses capacity expansion models that project long-term grid growth from fuel costs, demand, policy, and technology. Earth scientist Casey Burleyson will lead PNNL's part, which aims to build an AI model that picks out significant scenarios from the thousands produced and cuts computation time.

Other partners on that project are Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Pennsylvania State University, and the University of California San Diego. Both teams have six months to demonstrate their research goals, and the articles report that Burleyson and Elizondo are optimistic about the outcomes. The second team plans to test its AI-assisted model by comparing its output with that of a traditional capacity expansion model ensemble. Elizondo said the Genesis Mission lets the team try a technique that no one has tried before.

He also said some projections suggest the grid may need to be roughly double its current size to meet demand, while also integrating new technologies and loads. The articles present this as a reason the grid planning process itself needs rethinking. The articles describe PNNL as a laboratory operated by Battelle and supported by the Department of Energy's Office of Science, founded in 1965. They do not report any results from the projects, and they do not describe what happens after the six-month period beyond the demonstration of research goals.

Articles.Title: PNNL: Two Genesis Awards Support AI-Powered Grid Planning - HPCwire

stories.Headline: Inside the Lab: Can AI Solve the Critical Materials Challenge?
stories.Summary:
Researchers at Ames National Laboratory are using artificial intelligence to speed up the discovery of new materials, a field that technologies such as electric vehicles, wind turbines, fusion energy and defense systems depend on. The article, published on November 5, 2026, notes that finding and deploying new materials can take years or decades, while demand for them is growing quickly. Supply chains are also vulnerable to geopolitical pressure, limited resources and thin domestic processing capacity. The laboratory, which has a long history in rare earths and critical materials research, is combining AI with scientific expertise and experiments to address these problems.

The article describes several projects that apply this approach. Researchers are building AI-driven roadmaps toward what they call magnet sovereignty, meaning the ability to produce high-performance permanent magnets at home while balancing performance, cost and supply resilience. Their models combine experimental data with quantum-mechanical simulations to predict properties such as the Curie temperature, and the team validated predictions through synthesis of cerium-zirconium-iron alloys. In fusion energy, a platform called DuctGPT is being developed to screen structural alloys that can withstand extreme heat and neutron irradiation. A separate AI-enabled platform aims to recover cobalt and other critical metals from low-concentration sources such as mine tailings and wastewater, using designed biological systems.

The researchers say the work is meant to help scientists rather than replace them, since AI can sift large datasets and rank the most promising candidates for laboratory testing. The laboratory is also working with partners on producing battery-grade graphite from post-consumer textiles and has contributed to the Department of Energy's Critical Materials and Minerals to Unlock Supply initiative under the Genesis Mission. The article frames securing critical minerals as a systems problem that requires AI, advanced manufacturing, recycling and supply chain intelligence to work together. The authors state that AI alone will not solve the challenge. They present it as one of several tools that may help bring new materials into use more quickly.

Articles.Title: Inside the Lab: Can AI Solve the Critical Materials Challenge? - R&D World

stories.Headline: How Artificial Intelligence is reshaping accounting - KSNV
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence is changing the accounting profession, and this was the focus of Intuit Connect in Las Vegas, where the company's event highlighted how the technology is reshaping the work. News 3 spoke with Matt Wilpers, a Peloton instructor and former accountant, to learn why human involvement still matters in an industry being transformed by automation. The article was published on November 5, 2026, and was posted by KSNV, a Las Vegas station. The piece is short and centers on that single conversation. The article does not describe any new law, rule, or specific requirement.

It frames the change as a shift in how accounting work gets done, with automated tools taking on tasks that people once handled by hand. Its main point is that the human role remains important even as those tools spread through the field. The article does not provide figures, dates for any policy, or detailed examples of which tasks are being automated. The article attributes its perspective mainly to Matt Wilpers, who is identified as a Peloton instructor and former accountant. According to the piece, Wilpers was asked why people matter more than ever in an AI-driven world, and the article presents his views as the reason human judgment still counts.

The article does not name anyone else as responsible for the trend, and it does not include any statement from Intuit beyond the event itself. The surrounding page carries unrelated local news, including changes to short-term rental rules in Clark County and a ballot measure outcome in Nevada, but none of those items is connected to the accounting story. The article does not say what comes next for the technology, the event, or the profession. Any further developments would have to come from later reporting, and the piece itself offers no timeline or follow-up plans.

Articles.Title: How Artificial Intelligence is reshaping accounting - KSNV

stories.Headline: S2W Unveils AI Security Solutions at Germany's it-sa Expo
stories.Summary:
South Korean cybersecurity company S2W unveiled two AI security products at it-sa Expo & Congress 2026, a three-day exhibition held in Nuremberg, Germany, from October 27 to 29. The company presented XARVIS, an AI-powered security intelligence platform for government and public-sector organizations, and QUAXAR, an AI security solution for businesses and institutions. It-sa is one of Europe's leading information security exhibitions, and more than 1,000 companies took part this year. The event brings together cybersecurity companies and security professionals from the public and private sectors around the world.

XARVIS collects and analyzes criminal intelligence spread across the dark web, Telegram and social networking services to identify and profile threat actors. At the exhibition, S2W introduced DRI, or Deep Research Investigator, an investigation-focused AI agent that produces in-depth analytical findings through natural-language queries. DRI finds relevant information in large datasets based on user questions and combines detection and analytical tools to produce results. Users can retrieve information and carry out in-depth investigations in natural language without issuing complex commands for each analytical task. QUAXAR integrates and analyzes multiple sources of threat intelligence, including externally exposed assets, vulnerabilities, leaked account credentials and attacker activity.

By connecting previously fragmented threat information, QUAXAR assesses the likelihood of actual attacks and prioritizes responses by urgency. QUAXAR was supplied to a Greek government agency last year. During the exhibition, S2W held discussions with prospective customers and partners about possible cooperation. Building on its existing business experience in Europe, the company plans to assess local demand for AI-powered security and intelligence technologies and to expand its business opportunities across the region.

Articles.Title: S2W Unveils AI Security Solutions at Germany's it-sa Expo - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: LG Uplus, Seoul Women's University to Jointly Research AI Privacy Technologies
stories.Summary:
LG Uplus signed a memorandum of understanding with Seoul Women's University on November 2 at the university's campus in Nowon-gu, Seoul. The agreement covers joint research and professional training in personal information protection, AI and data. Attendees included Hong Kwan-hee, head of LG Uplus' Information Security Center, Lee Yoon-sun, president of Seoul Women's University, and Kim Hyung-jong, chair of the Department of Personal Information Protection at the university's graduate school. The two parties will use the Innovation Zone, being established at Seoul Women's University by the Personal Information Protection Commission, as a research hub for technologies that combine and analyze pseudonymized data.

They plan to study secure ways to integrate public and private-sector data, including telecommunications data, and assess the risk of re-identifying individuals before and after data integration. The partners will test technologies that automatically detect and pseudonymize sensitive information using actual datasets. They will also research Privacy by Design, an approach that incorporates personal information protection principles from the initial planning and design stages of services, with the aim of applying the technology to telecommunications services in the future. The agreement also includes cooperation on professional training.

LG Uplus will participate in Seoul Women's University's graduate-level programs to train master's and doctoral specialists in personal information protection and data utilization. The company plans to provide curriculum advice, capstone projects and joint seminars, as well as lectures by industry professionals, thesis supervision and practical mentoring. Hong said that by combining the university's specialized research capabilities with LG Uplus' practical industry experience, the company will strengthen its competitiveness in information security and contribute to training the next generation of security professionals needed by industry. LG Uplus has increased investment in information security and expanded efforts to recruit specialists following a personal information breach in 2023.

At the time, the company announced a cybersecurity innovation plan and pledged to raise its annual information security investment to around 100 billion won. Its actual information security investment in 2023 was provisionally estimated at approximately 114.4 billion won. In the same year, LG Uplus signed an agreement with Soongsil University to establish an employment-linked Department of Information Security. The department admitted its first class of 20 students in 2024 and is scheduled to produce its first graduates in 2028.

Articles.Title: LG Uplus, Seoul Women's University to Jointly Research AI Privacy Technologies - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: DEEPX, AMD Discuss AI Chip Technology Cooperation
stories.Summary:
DEEPX, a fabless semiconductor company that specializes in edge artificial intelligence chips, said on Nov. 3 that it had discussed potential technology cooperation with AMD. Keith Strier, AMD's senior vice president of global AI markets, and Jang Jung-hee, head of AMD Korea, visited DEEPX's headquarters in Pangyo that day. They met with DEEPX CEO Kim Nok-won to discuss possible collaboration in physical AI and heterogeneous computing. The talks between the two companies began at the AMD-Korean AI Semiconductor Companies Roundtable hosted by the Ministry of Science and ICT on Oct. 7. DEEPX proposed two areas of cooperation.

The first involves integrating its low-power neural processing unit with AMD's Kria system-on-module platform, which would let a single module handle real-time robotic control and AI inference. The second involves linking AMD's ROCm software platform for graphics processing units with DEEPX's software development kit. The goal is a computing environment that distributes workloads among central processing units, GPUs and NPUs according to their respective strengths. At the October roundtable, AMD CEO Lisa Su met with Kim, and AMD Korea representatives visited DEEPX on Oct. 21.

The Nov. 3 meeting at Pangyo followed those earlier contacts. The article does not say whether the two companies reached any agreement or set a timeline for further talks. It also gives no date for when any cooperation might begin. More to follow.

Articles.Title: DEEPX, AMD Discuss AI Chip Technology Cooperation - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Anthropic Unveils Open-Source Technology to Verify AI Outputs
stories.Summary:
Anthropic announced on Nov. 3 through its official blog that it is developing a system called FlashProve, which it describes as provable inference. The company said the technology attaches cryptographic proofs to AI-generated outputs so users can verify whether a response came from the model they believed they were using. Anthropic compared the approach to the digital signatures used to confirm the sender of an email. The researchers also released detailed technical specifications and working code, which is available on GitHub under an open-source license.

FlashProve is designed to address cases in which even the company developing and operating a model tries to pass off another model as the claimed one. If commercialized, it could stop AI service providers from secretly substituting cheaper, less capable models for the high-performance models users requested. It could also verify claims that a more expensive, higher-performance model was used when companies inflate performance evaluations or benchmark results. The technology has four key properties: completeness, which accepts valid proofs, soundness, which rejects forged proofs, succinctness, which enables verification on ordinary PCs using small proof files, and zero knowledge, which proves output provenance without revealing model weights.

Implementing FlashProve requires AI model developers to publish a fingerprint for each model before its release, and the fingerprint does not reveal the model's weights. Anthropic says this allows the technology to be applied not only to open-source models but also to commercial models whose weights remain private. The verification process is designed to be lightweight enough to run directly on users' devices without large-scale computing infrastructure. The researchers emphasized that the release is a progress update rather than completed research, and they said the technology was made public so other researchers can examine, use and further develop it.

The technology remains under development, and no plans have been announced to deploy it in Anthropic's services or those of other AI companies. In current enterprise AI services, users often cannot independently verify which model generated a response, even when accessing models through APIs or cloud platforms. If a service provider changes models or routes requests to different models, users may have difficulty detecting the change. As enterprise AI adoption expands and environments increasingly combine multiple models, tools such as FlashProve could support verification of AI service contracts and service-level agreements.

Articles.Title: Anthropic Unveils Open-Source Technology to Verify AI Outputs - www.thelec.net

stories.Headline: Cammsys Begins Mass Production of Cameras for Samsung AI Refrigerators
stories.Summary:
Cammsys said on Nov. 4 that it has begun mass production of camera modules for Samsung Electronics' artificial intelligence refrigerators. The company will start supplying ultra-wide-angle and AI camera modules this month for all models of Samsung's Bespoke AI Family Hub refrigerators. This is Cammsys' first mass production of camera modules for home appliances, after a business focused on smartphones. The supply agreement marks its first mass-production revenue in the home appliance sector.

Cammsys is applying design and mass-production technologies it developed for smartphone camera modules to home appliances. The company is also working with Samsung Electronics' Digital Appliances division to develop cameras for home appliances other than refrigerators. Because appliance cameras often keep the same specifications over long supply periods, the business could reduce revenue volatility compared with mobile camera modules. In non-mobile applications, Cammsys is also developing cameras for robotics and security.

A Cammsys official said the company will continue development cooperation with Samsung Electronics and expand the range of home appliances using its camera modules that can be supplied over the long term. The official also said Cammsys will pursue new business opportunities in non-mobile sectors, including robotics. The company is pursuing supplies of facial recognition cameras. It is also participating in the camera-related supply chain for the hands of Hyundai Motor Group's Atlas humanoid robot.

Articles.Title: Cammsys Begins Mass Production of Cameras for Samsung AI Refrigerators - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Hyosung to Supply Cooling Pumps for SKT’s Ulsan AI Data Center
stories.Summary:
Hyosung Goodsprings, a pump manufacturing subsidiary of Hyosung Group, will supply high-efficiency cooling pumps for SK Telecom's artificial intelligence data center in Ulsan. The company has secured orders covering the Ulsan data center's 100-megawatt capacity, according to industry sources cited on Nov. 4. The contracts cover sensorless inline pumps for both the 40MW first-phase facility, Building A, and the 60MW second-phase facility, Building B. The pumps regulate the circulation of cooling water used to dissipate heat generated by servers. The sensorless inline pumps automatically adjust motor speeds according to server cooling loads, running faster when cooling demand rises and slower when it falls.

This avoids continuous operation at maximum output and reduces unnecessary power consumption, and the pumps also control operating conditions without separate flow sensors, simplifying equipment configuration and maintenance. The integrated inverters are supplied by ABB, a Swedish-Swiss power technology company, and Hyosung Goodsprings has added a total harmonic distortion monitoring function so operators can check electrical conditions without separate measuring equipment. A 40MW data center typically requires about 20 to 30 pumps, so the 100MW Ulsan facility would need more than 50. With a set of pumps for a 40MW facility costing approximately 1.5 billion won, the total supply value for the Ulsan data center is estimated at around 4 billion won.

SK Telecom plans to expand its domestic AI data center investments starting with Ulsan, with clusters exceeding 2GW in the Yeongnam region and 1GW in the southwestern region. The company intends to gradually expand domestic capacity to 5GW starting in 2029, with a goal of 15GW by 2035. Applying the same cooling equipment requirements, the total demand for pumps could reach approximately 600 billion won, and Hyosung Goodsprings could see substantial revenue growth if it secures additional orders for SK Telecom's future data centers. The company's revenue declined slightly to 230.1 billion won last year from 236.3 billion won a year earlier, while operating profit increased approximately 48% to 20.9 billion won from 14.2 billion won over the same period.

Hyosung Goodsprings has also secured several domestic data center operators as customers beyond SK Telecom, supplying cooling pumps to the 35MW Deogi-dong Internet Data Center in Ilsan, the 80MW GPC IDC in Hwaseong, the 50MW TIMBUKTU IDC in Ansan and the 25MW Global Cloud Center IDC in Ansan. The company is an unlisted, wholly owned subsidiary of Hyosung specializing in industrial pump manufacturing, and it also produces large industrial pumps for oil refining, petrochemical facilities and power plants, as well as pumps for nuclear power plants. Its major customers include ExxonMobil and Aramco. Cooling systems account for approximately 40% of a facility's total energy consumption, which the article says makes pump efficiency important for reducing operating costs.

Articles.Title: Hyosung to Supply Cooling Pumps for SKT’s Ulsan AI Data Center - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: AMD, FuriosaAI and MangoBoost to Build AI Infrastructure Cluster in 2027
stories.Summary:
AMD announced on Nov. 4, 2026, that it will partner with FuriosaAI and MangoBoost to build a heterogeneous artificial intelligence computing infrastructure cluster in Seoul next year. Keith Strier, AMD's senior vice president of global AI markets, announced the plan at the AMD Advancing AI Seoul 2026 event held at the Westin Seoul Parnas in Samseong-dong. He said the three companies will sign a memorandum of understanding shortly. He said the first reference cluster is planned for Seoul next spring, using heterogeneous AI computing infrastructure that integrates processors from all three companies.

Heterogeneous computing combines different types of semiconductors to improve computational efficiency. The platform will integrate AMD's central processing units and graphics processing units with FuriosaAI's neural processing units and MangoBoost's data processing units. FuriosaAI develops its proprietary Renegade NPU, a chip designed for AI inference in data centers, and began mass production of its second-generation RNGD in January this year. FuriosaAI claims the chip delivers 1.7 to 1.8 times the performance of Nvidia's H100 at the same power consumption, and it has signed a technology validation agreement with LG AI Research and supplied chips to Upstage. MangoBoost's DPU is called BoostX, and it handles communications, storage input and output and security processing in AI infrastructure.

Integrating AMD hardware with Korean-made semiconductors was among the initiatives in a memorandum of understanding signed by AMD and South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT at the AI Summit in San Francisco in July this year. The two sides agreed to jointly develop and demonstrate heterogeneous AI computing infrastructure combining AMD chips with Korean AI NPUs. AMD CEO Lisa Su further detailed the initiative during her visit to South Korea in October, and she pledged to develop the infrastructure into a reference model for use in global markets. AMD also announced plans to establish an AI Center of Excellence with the Ministry of Science and ICT, and it plans to announce additional partnerships with Korean companies.

Articles.Title: AMD, FuriosaAI and MangoBoost to Build AI Infrastructure Cluster in 2027 - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: KAI to Develop AI Agent to Improve Weapon System Efficiency
stories.Summary:
Korea Aerospace Industries said on Nov. 4 that it will develop an artificial intelligence agent that combines AI with military logistics big data. The company held a kickoff meeting for the project at the Daejeon Convention Center that day, with 100 participants. Attendees included representatives from the Ministry of National Defense, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources, the Institute of Civil-Military Technology Cooperation of the Agency for Defense Development, and government officials. KAI was selected as the lead research and development organization in September.

The project is called RAM-C AI agent development, and RAM-C stands for Reliability, Availability, Maintainability and Cost. It is an interministerial cooperative technology development initiative funded by the Ministry of National Defense and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources and overseen by the Institute of Civil-Military Technology Cooperation. The project has a total budget of 29.3 billion won and will run for four years. The aim is to improve the accuracy of RAM-C analysis by integrating and analyzing maintenance and operational data across the entire life cycle of weapon systems, from acquisition and operation to maintenance and performance upgrades.

KAI will build an integrated military logistics data analytics platform that uses AI to support forecasting and decision-making. The AI will manage total maintenance costs and component payment schedules throughout the life cycle of complex weapon systems, including fighter jets and tanks, from development to retirement. KAI will form a domestic consortium to conduct phased demonstrations using actual operational, maintenance and sensor data from representative weapon systems across the Army, Navy and Air Force. The company will verify the applicability of core technologies in operational environments and establish a unified framework for deployment across the armed forces.

Park Kyung-eun, head of KAI’s Customer Support Division, said the project is significant because it will enable the company to secure data-driven military logistics decision-making technologies. He said these technologies combine logistics data with AI to improve weapon system availability and operational efficiency. Once development is completed, the technology is expected to prevent operational disruptions caused by equipment failures, maximizing weapon system availability and operational efficiency. It is also expected to strengthen competitiveness in follow-on logistics support, including maintenance and spare parts services provided to overseas customers after weapon delivery.

Articles.Title: KAI to Develop AI Agent to Improve Weapon System Efficiency - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: AI’s Off-Balance-Sheet Bill Tops $4.1 Trillion: Should You Be Concerned?
stories.Summary:
Intel's shares fell as much as 30% during trading on 30 October, dropping as low as $64.24 and wiping out nearly $150 billion in market value, its worst single day since the 1970s. The sell-off followed fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $15 billion to $16 billion, more than $1 billion below analysts' average estimate of about $17 billion. Chief financial officer David Zinsner said the company does not expect positive cash flow this year, and an incident at its Israeli factory is expected to cut fourth-quarter revenue by roughly $300 million. PC shipments are projected to fall about 12% this year and another 10% in 2027. Until 29 October, Intel's stock had at one point gained nearly 150% on the year as investors treated it as an AI beneficiary.

The articles tie that episode to a larger tally of $4.11 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments, made up of non-cancellable purchase commitments, signed leases not yet started, and guarantees for data centre and chip projects. Meta's purchase commitments rose to $455 billion from $349 billion, its not-yet-commenced leases to $356 billion from $279 billion, and its residual value guarantees for the Hyperion and El Paso ventures came to $41.5 billion. Amazon's unconditional purchase obligations nearly doubled to $254 billion from $130 billion, with commitments up $131 billion, or 41%, in one quarter. Alphabet's total reached $1.059 trillion, the first single company above $1 trillion, while Microsoft grew by $35 billion, or 6%. SpaceX's commitments climbed from $29 billion to $51 billion by 26 October, a rise of 174%.

Against these commitments, the companies carry about $1 trillion in recognised debt and lease liabilities, so the off-balance-sheet total is more than four times as large. The total was about $1.8 trillion at the end of June, $3.12 trillion by the end of August and $4.11 trillion in October. Among the five companies that had reported third-quarter results, the combined figure rose to $3.05 trillion from $2.48 trillion, an addition of $577 billion, or 23%. Meta, rated Aa3/AA-, saw its credit default swaps hit a record after earnings and announced plans to raise up to $95 billion in equity, of which $37.5 billion was already raised. S&P cut Meta's outlook to negative from stable on 30 October while keeping the AA- rating, citing AI spending, negative free cash flow and lease obligations of $355.7 billion.

The articles note that S&P adjusts leverage for off-balance-sheet leases while Moody's and Fitch do not, a point raised by Goldman Sachs credit strategist Amanda Lynam. Mark Habib of S&P Global warned that implicit guarantees for data centres and smaller AI firms could leave hyperscalers with large undisclosed debt, and guarantees from US technology giants over the past year have reached up to $300 billion. The Bank for International Settlements has warned that opaque AI financing adds to financial vulnerabilities, with circular financing the biggest risk. The articles argue the danger lies in inflexible cash outflows set against uncertain revenue, since weak rental income could push project companies into shortfalls and force parent companies to step in. The text breaks off before saying what happens next.

Articles.Title: U.S. Big Tech’s AI Off-Balance-Sheet Commitments Surge 90% to $3.2 Trillion - Businesskorea
